### P18-23 group attacks decided (2026-11-07)

- Owner (2026-11-01, tasklist line, quoted): "group special attacks like Urban Reign (two on one, one grabs and one attacks)"; task text: "The attack list has at least these two: one fighter grabs the target and the other hits it; both strike one target. Anyone can start one: people, CPU allies and CPU enemies." Decided by the coordinator's delegate under the owner's standing go ("balanced", "select the correct option"); every "Decided" line can be changed by the owner. Our own design from the P18-22 findings (no Urban Reign names, moves or look). P18-24 builds it after P18-21 (goons, allies). Nothing here changes the game code.
- What the code does today (base 8aa8c39, `breakpoint.html` 1,178,607 bytes counted as LF + BOM, the budget's measure; 1,194,739 on disk with CRLF):
  - The holding half exists. A grab (`startClinch`, :7241) puts the grabber in `S.GRAPPLE` and the victim in `S.CLINCH`, linked by `partner`. The holder may strike twice (`CLINCH_STRIKE_MAX` 2: elbow 7, knee 5 with a 10 stamina drain; `CLINCH_STRIKE_COOLDOWN` 22) or throw (10 to 21 damage, `THROW_SETS` and the style throws). The victim escapes with Grapple from tick `CLINCH_ESCAPE_FROM` 12 (rear 14) if it has `ESCAPE_STAMINA` 6; an early press costs 10 stamina and a 24-tick lock (`tryEscape`, :6257); a hold times out at `CLINCH_MAX` 110.
  - The hitting half is missing on purpose: `Combat.strikable` (:6933) refuses a fighter in `S.CLINCH` or `S.GRAPPLE`, and `evaluate` refuses a grab on either of them. So a hold is closed to everybody, the holder included (nobody can rescue a victim by hitting the holder; that stays).
  - Teams: `Fighter.team` 0 = players, 1 = enemies; a lineup gives every free-for-all slot its own team, so "teammate" is simply "same `team`". `MatchSim.canHurt` (:9945) lets teammates hurt each other only with Friendly fire (a person, or any player in a crowd fight). A CPU never hurts a teammate.
  - Flow of a tick: `readIntents`, `updateFighters`, `resolveCombat` (:11177: strikes first, grabs after, alternating start index), so a new move type slots in without a new phase. A Grapple press goes through `bufferInput` and `tryBufferedAttack` (:5821) into `startGrab`; a Grapple press next to a held fighter is today a grab that whiffs (9 + 3 + 24 ticks).
  - The CPU: `AIController.thinkGrapple` (:9320) throws after 8 to 27 ticks (`clinchPlan.at`), `thinkClinched` (:9334) escapes by roll, and `CrowdDirector` gives attack tokens per target (`BRAWL_ATTACK_TOKENS` Easy 1, Normal 2, Hard 2, Expert 3; the holder keeps its token until the hold ends).
  - Combo ownership: `claimCombo` resets the victim's combo count when a different attacker hits, so two teammates taking turns on one fighter already avoid the combo damage scale (`COMBO_SCALE`). That is a free team bonus that exists today; it is why the new numbers below stay small.
  - Thrown bodies (P18-25 + P18-32): a flying body hurts what its thrower may hurt (`canHurt`), so it never hurts the thrower's teammates unless Friendly fire is on; the helper of a group hold is therefore safe from the throw that ends it.
  - Fingerprints: every recorded hash is a 1v1 (P18-25's note); a 1v1 has no teammate, so nothing below can move one.
- Decided: two team attacks, both built from rules the game already has, with no new on-screen button, no new binding and no meter. They are called PIN SHOT (a teammate hits the fighter that someone is holding) and CROSSFIRE (two teammates hit one fighter from opposite sides). The table of answers:

  | # | Question | Decided |
  |---|---|---|
  | 1 | Attack list | PIN SHOT (one fighter grabs, the other hits the held fighter) and CROSSFIRE (both strike one target). Nothing else |
  | 2 | Trigger | PIN SHOT: the helper presses the existing Grapple input (GRAB on touch, R2 / R3 / right-stick flick on a pad, G or Numpad 3 on the keyboard, the seat 3 and 4 keys too) while a held enemy is within reach. CROSSFIRE: no input at all, it is what two ordinary strikes do when they land together |
  | 3 | Who | any fighter on a team with a teammate: people, CPU allies (P18-21), CPU enemies (goons and bosses). The holder is anybody who grabbed; the helper is a different fighter of the holder's team; the victim is on a different team than both. Friendly fire never makes a teammate a victim of a team attack |
  | 4 | Cost | PIN SHOT: 8 stamina for the helper, a 240-tick cooldown for the helper, and the victim cannot be pin-shotted again for 300 ticks. CROSSFIRE: free, but a 180-tick lock on the victim. No meter, no momentum cost |
  | 5 | The victim's way out | unchanged: Grapple from tick 12 (rear 14), 6 stamina; a pin shot can never take the victim's stamina below 6; a clean escape also shoves the helper off |
  | 6 | Damage cap | PIN SHOT hits once per hold for 10 (base); with the holder's two clinch strikes the hold deals at most 24 before the throw (31 with P18-06's CL rider). CROSSFIRE adds x1.25 to the second hit only |
  | 7 | Modes | every mode that has a team of two or more: Free Fight (2v2 and up, Brawl, Co-op, lineups), Versus teams, Arcade brawls with the story ally, Survival brawls with allies, and CPU groups against a person. Not in 1v1, a free-for-all, the Tournament (1v1) or Training (no teammate) |
  | 8 | Setting | one Free Fight rule row "Team attacks" (Off, On), default On |
  | 9 | Determinism | no new random draw in the sim; the CPU rolls once per hold with `simRng`, only when a pin shot is possible |

#### PIN SHOT (one holds, one hits)

- Roles. Holder: the fighter in `S.GRAPPLE` with a `partner` in `S.CLINCH` (it keeps all its options: two clinch strikes, throw, let go). Victim: the `S.CLINCH` fighter. Helper: a free fighter of the holder's team (idle, walking, running, crouching or guarding, i.e. every state where `updateFree` lets it start an attack). The holder never needs to do anything for the helper; people holding just play as today.
- Trigger, all devices. The helper's Grapple press is buffered as today. At `tryBufferedAttack`, before `startGrab`, `Combat.assistTarget(f, match)` looks for a victim; when it finds one the press starts the helper's PIN SHOT move instead of a grab, otherwise the press is a grab as always. A press next to a held enemy used to be a whiffed grab, so no working input is taken away. Eligibility (all must hold, no random number): the helper is alive and not carrying; `match.live` and `teamAttacks`; the victim is `S.CLINCH`, alive, its `partner` is in `S.GRAPPLE` and on the helper's team and is not the helper; the victim's team differs from the helper's (so Friendly fire is irrelevant); the footing differs by at most `GRAB_LEDGE` 0.55; the centre-to-centre distance is at most `ASSIST_REACH` 1.8 m (the move steps 0.3 m, reach 1.3 m); the victim's `clinchTick` is at least `escapeStartFor(victim)` (12, rear 14) at the press, so the 8-tick wind-up always runs inside an escape window that is already open (a person who presses on hold tick 1 would otherwise land the kick at about tick 9, before the victim can escape at all; a press earlier than that tick stays a plain grab, as today); the helper has `ASSIST_STAMINA` 8 (below it the press is the normal grab, the stamina bar already flashes `lowStamina`); `helper.assistCd` is 0; `victim.assistLock` is 0 and this hold has had no pin shot yet. If two helpers' pin shots go active on the same tick, `evaluate` (no side effects; `resolveCombat` evaluates every attacker before it applies any, :11186-11202) returns a descriptor for both; `Combat.apply` (case `assist`) checks `victim.assisted` again and makes the later one a whiff, and "later" follows `resolveCombat`'s existing alternating start index (`tick % count`), not the fighter index. The victim is the nearest eligible one, ties to the lower fighter index.
- The move. A normal attack-state move, so the existing frame machinery, hit list, animation, interrupt and hit-stop all apply, and the victim, the holder and everybody else can see it coming:

  | Field | Value |
  |---|---|
  | id / name | `assist` / "Pin Shot" |
  | type, ctx | `assist`, `assist` (a new type: not `strike`, not `grab`, so no chain, no string and no counter rule reads it) |
  | startup / active / recovery (ticks) | 8 / 3 / 20 |
  | base damage, stamina | 10, 8 |
  | reach, width, step | 1.3, 0.7, 0.3 (the same measure as the other moves: reach x the helper's reach stat + the victim's radius) |
  | animation | an existing kick animation (the push or side kick), limb RL; no new pose data. The helper faces the victim from the first tick (`aim` = the victim, as a running attack does) |
  | victim stamina drain | 8, never below `ESCAPE_STAMINA` 6 (if the victim has less than 6 already it is left as it is) |
  | event | `hit` with `mv` { id 'assist', name 'Pin Shot', tier 2, cat 'kick', h 'M', kind 'hit', hitStop 6 }, then `teamHit` { kind 'pin' } |

  Because the helper is in `S.ATTACK`, a hit on the helper in its startup cancels the pin shot (that is the counter-play for the victim's own team: strike the helper); the helper's own stamina, exhaust and speed rules apply as for any move.
- What it hits. `evaluate` returns `{ type: 'assist' }` only for the helper's `assist` move against a fighter that still meets the eligibility test above at the active frame (still `S.CLINCH`, same holder, still within reach and ledge). If the victim has escaped, been thrown, been knocked out or let go, the move finds nobody: a whiff, with the full recovery. `strikable` keeps refusing everybody else, so a normal Punch or Kick, a thrown item or a flying body still cannot touch a held fighter, and nobody else can hit it: the exception is that one move against that one situation. `apply` runs a new `Combat.assistHit`.
- Damage. `assistHit` uses the same formula as `clinchStrike` (:7284), so one helper function (`heldHit(att, def, dmg, drain, match)`) serves both and the copy is avoided: damage = 10 x the helper's damage stat x boost x (0.6 if the helper was out of stamina) x `comboScale(def.gotHits)` x the victim's `taken`, rounded to 0.1, at least 1, held up by `floorHp`; `claimCombo`, `momentum`, `knockOut` and the credit (`lastFoe`) work as for a clinch strike. The victim stays in `S.CLINCH` (no hit reaction), flashes, and the hit-stop is 6. A KO by a pin shot ends the hold at once (the holder's `updateGrapple` already lets go when the victim leaves `S.CLINCH`).
- Caps and locks (all measured in match ticks, kept in fields set on the fighters in `startClinch` and `assistHit`): one pin shot per hold; the helper's `assistCd` 240 after it starts one (whiffs included); the victim's `assistLock` 300 after it was hit by one (so a pack of goons cannot chain holds into pin shots, and a person is never pinned and hit again within 5 s). The holder's two clinch strikes and its throw are untouched. The most one hold can deal before the throw is 7 + 7 + 10 = 24 (all x the fighters' stats); the throw adds 10 to 21. Against 90 to 135 health (`deriveStats`, :4319; the Health rule scales it by 0.5 to 2, and a Half-health fight makes the cap 36 to 53 percent of a fighter) that is about 18 to 27 percent at Normal health. With the Clinch rider of P18-06 (3 clinch strikes, KELSEY and GIORGI) the cap is 7 + 7 + 7 + 10 = 31, about 23 to 34 percent.
- The victim's escape. Decided: the window and the cost stay exactly as today (opens at tick 12, rear 14; 6 stamina; an early press costs 10 and a 24-tick lock), because P18-22 found that the complaint about the genre is an unclear escape, not a weak one. Added: (1) the stamina floor above, so a pin shot can never make the escape impossible; (2) when the escape succeeds, a helper within 1.4 m of the pair is shoved away at 4 m/s (no damage, no stagger, its move continues and whiffs) - this is the "answer that moves both attackers" the reviews describe, in its smallest form. Because a pin shot can only start once the window is open (eligibility above), the victim always has the whole 8-tick wind-up to press Grapple: a person who reads the helper's wind-up and presses at once gets out before the hit lands; one who waits takes a 10-damage kick. That is the intended read, and it holds for a person helper too (co-op, 2v2), not only for the CPU, whose reaction delay already puts its hit at tick 17 or later. The hit may still land one tick after a press made on its active frame (same tick order as any strike against an escape); that is accepted.
- The CPU as helper (allies and enemies): in `AIController.chooseIntent`, after the `S.CLINCH` and `S.GRAPPLE` branches and before the plans, a new `thinkAssist(f, match, it)`:
  1. It looks for a victim by the same `Combat.assistTarget` test, relaxed on distance to `ASSIST_JOIN_DIST` 3.5 m (it walks in; it uses the AI's existing walk-to-target code with the victim as target and presses Grapple once within `ASSIST_REACH`; no new navigation).
  2. Per hold it rolls once, with `simRng`, whether it joins: Easy 0.3, Normal 0.55, Hard 0.8, Expert 1.0 (`ASSIST_JOIN` table), and not before `d.react` ticks after the clinch began (20 / 14 / 10 / 8), so its hit lands at tick 17 to 29 of the hold. The roll key is the hold (`holdId` of the holder, set in `startClinch`), so it is drawn once per hold per helper and never in a fight with no hold, no teammate or `teamAttacks` off: no random number is drawn outside a situation where a pin shot is possible, so every fight that cannot have one plays bit for bit as before.
  3. Tokens: an engaged AI (one that shares its target with another AI) joins only while it holds an attack token, so the crowd rules cap it by difficulty with no new constant: Easy has one token, which the holder keeps, so two CPU enemies never pin-shot a person on Easy; Normal and Hard allow one helper; Expert allows two to walk in, but only the first lands (one pin shot per hold; the second is a whiff, see the apply check above). An AI that is not engaged (an ally next to a person) needs none.
  4. It needs at least `AI_GRAB_STAMINA` 0.3 of its stamina and the cooldown at 0, like a grab.
  The AI holder waits for a helper: when a legal helper has rolled "joins" and is within `ASSIST_JOIN_DIST`, the holder's `clinchPlan.at` is raised once to `ASSIST_HOLD_WAIT` 32 ticks (no random draw), so its first strike or throw does not come before the kick; the hold still ends by the existing rules, at the latest at `CLINCH_MAX`.
- Taking part as a person: nothing to learn beyond Grapple. A person who holds an enemy plays as before; a teammate (person or CPU) who is near can kick. A CPU ally with a person as the holder joins by the rules above; a person next to a CPU ally's hold presses Grapple. In Co-op (up to 4 seats) every seat can do either.

#### CROSSFIRE (both strike one target)

- What it is. When one fighter's landed strike is followed within `CROSSFIRE_WINDOW` 24 ticks by a landed strike from a teammate of the first attacker, from the other side of the target, the second hit is a CROSSFIRE: x`CROSSFIRE_MULT` 1.25 damage (before the stats and the target's `taken`), and a `teamHit` { kind 'crossfire' } event. It is not a new move: any strike, string step or kick counts, so the CPU, which already spreads its fighters round a target (`CrowdDirector` ring spots), and the people use it without a thought, and a person who deliberately flanks is rewarded.
- Conditions (all, deterministic, checked in `landHit` before the damage is worked out): `match.teamAttacks`; the first hit was a landed, unblocked, un-swayed strike (`landHit`; a block, a sway, a clinch strike, a pin shot, a thrown item, a thrown body, a tackle and a ground hit do not count and do not open the window); the two attackers are different fighters on the same team; the target is on a different team from both (Friendly fire never makes a teammate a target); the angle at the target between the two attackers is at least 100 degrees (`CROSSFIRE_COS` -0.17 on the dot product of the unit vectors from the target to each); the target is not in a clinch or hold and is not being thrown; the target's `crossfireLock` is 0. After a crossfire the target is locked for `CROSSFIRE_LOCK` 180 ticks (3 s): no second crossfire, so a pack cannot loop it. The window starts from a new pair of fields on the target (`lastStrikeBy`, `lastStrikeTick`) that every landed strike writes (two assignments).
- Reaction: none new. The second hit uses its own move's reaction (hit, stagger, knockdown), so a crossfire by a heavy kick is a knockdown as it already is, a jab a flinch. Bonus damage only, because the knockdown for every crossfire (the first idea) would turn a goon pack's every second hit on a person into a knockdown; rejected.
- Reading it: the victim is hit from both sides; a person who sees two attackers on opposite sides can step out (sidestep, jump) or guard (a block only covers the side the fighter faces, which is the existing `facing` test); the stamina, the lock and the 1.25 factor are the whole cost to learn.

#### Interactions

- Friendly fire. It is a separate setting and stays so: it still governs ordinary strikes, grabs, tackles and thrown bodies between teammates. A team attack's victim is always an enemy of both fighters, with Friendly fire on or off. Examples: a person holds a teammate under Friendly fire - nobody may pin-shot it, and its teammate cannot "join" the hold; a person strikes a teammate under Friendly fire and a second teammate strikes the same fighter - no crossfire. A CPU never hurts a teammate, flag or not, as today.
- Free Fight rules (P18-42 decided, P18-43 built as `FIGHT_RULES`, :690): one new row, "Team attacks", values Off and On, default On, stored as `rules.team` (0 or 1, a new field with a default, `v` stays 1; a missing or bad value reads as On), becomes `cfg.teamAttacks`. Shown on "More options" after Health (index 6 of `FIGHT_RULES`, before Player 1 starts); dimmed "Not used: nobody has a teammate". Friendly fire is a lineup row, not a `FightRules` row (:14035), so the new row reuses its test, `MatchLineup.hasTeammates(lineup)` (:14015), inside `FightRules.why`; a stored Off is kept while the row is dimmed. All four presets (Standard, Tournament bout, Survival style, Ring match) set On, so they stay comparable; the Tournament is 1v1 and unaffected. The label rule is unchanged (the first preset whose rows equal the current ones, ignoring dimmed rows). Arcade and Survival always play with it On (they have no rules screen). Rematch repeats the `cfg`, so it is kept. The other rows do not interact: Health, Items, Hazards and Breakables only change numbers or scenery; a helper holding a weapon puts it down when it presses Grapple, as a grab does (`dropBothHands`); Ring-out does not matter because a hold does not move the pair and a thrown victim cannot hurt the helper (the thrower's team is exempt). Square ring and walls: the helper steps at most 0.3 m, the existing wall rules apply.
- Free-for-all and Versus: a free-for-all has no teammate, so nothing happens. A 2v2 team lineup is the main case.
- Brawls with allies (P18-20 + P18-37): allies are CPU fighters of `TEAM_PLAYERS` that take no orders; they join a person's hold by the CPU rules above, and an enemy crew can do it to a person or to an ally. Loss and win rules, the "every person down" rule and the stamina edge (`giveStaminaEdge` skips allies) are not touched. A held ally is as pin-shot-able as a person.
- P18-06 (abilities, draft in `decide\P18-06.md`): with the CL rider (3 clinch strikes: KELSEY, GIORGI) the hold cap is 31, not 24 (see Caps); a TB rider (for example DMITRI's Heavy Hands) moves the escape by 1 tick; the pin shot's tick floor uses `escapeStartFor(victim)`, so it follows the TB change automatically and a pin shot still never starts before the escape is open. Nothing else in P18-06 touches a team attack; P18-24 re-checks the numbers if P18-06 changes the clinch.
- Stats and grades: the damage is ordinary damage with the helper as the attacker (`hit` event), so the existing per-move totals, combo counters and grade inputs count it; no new `Progress` stat or grade rule. The one new saved field is the tip flag `seenTeam`.
- Replays and online: all of it is inside the fixed 60 Hz tick, reads only `cfg` and fighter state, uses the tick counters and the fighter order, and draws a random number only in the CPU's once-per-hold join roll. `teamAttacks` is a `cfg` field (missing = on) so a host sends it with the rest and a `JSON` round trip of the `cfg` gives the same fight. `SimRunner.run` passes the new field through by name.

#### On screen, sound, tip

- Camera: no cut and no zoom; the existing `Camera.impact` is used: 0.45 / 0.35 on a pin shot, 0.5 / 0.4 on a crossfire. The hit-stop is 6 on both.
- Flash and floor cue: the pin shot uses the existing hit spark and flash from the `hit` event (tier 2) and adds a `FX.ring` under the victim in the helper's team tint; the crossfire adds the same ring at the target. When a hold starts and a helper is already in reach, the `clinch` event carries `help: true` and the ring is drawn once at the victim's feet in the holder's team tint, so people on both sides can see the hold is open to a kick (one ring, no text).
- Pop-ups: the existing `popAt` shows PIN SHOT or CROSSFIRE (white, larger for 400 ms) at the victim, next to the damage pop that the `hit` event already makes.
- Sound: the hit sound of the `hit` event plus one short rising two-note `tone` (triangle, about 330 to 520 Hz, 0.08 s) so the team hit is heard as such; gamepad rumble for the person who is hit through the existing `hit` hook.
- Hint and tip (once only, saved as `Progress.d.seenTeam`, written like `seenClinch`): the first time a person is a helper-in-reach, the hint line over the fighter (the existing `grappleHint` element) reads "PIN SHOT: press GRAB to hit the held fighter" (touch label GRAB, pad R2, keyboard G, taken from `keyName('grapple', seat)` like the clinch hint); the first time a person is on the receiving end, the clinch hint already says what to do. After that no text: the floor ring is the permanent cue. The Controls help page gets one short paragraph "Team attacks" (what Pin Shot and Crossfire are and that Grapple triggers the first), in the place where Holds are described (:14243).

#### Rejected

- A new button or a gesture for the helper: P17-06's no-clutter rule, and Grapple next to a hold was an empty input.
- Letting a normal Punch or Kick hit a held fighter: it would let any launcher or knockdown pull the victim out of the hold and break the holder's grapple; a fixed move cannot.
- Letting the victim's team hit the holder to rescue (the genre's usual answer): holders are unhittable today and a grab is a safe move in a crowd; changing that moves P14-01 and the whole Brawl balance. Owner may ask for it later.
- A tag-throw with a toss and a catch (the Urban Reign-style launch-and-slam): needs a catch state for the helper, a body in flight that a teammate may touch and a landing rule; the thrown-body rules already make a throw into a crowd count. Left as a possible later task.
- Orders to the ally (P1-03 rejected them) and a cooperative input for two people at once: a two-person press at the right time was the fiddly part of the genre's co-op moves.
- A team meter or momentum cost: no source gives one; the cooldown and stamina cost need no new UI.
- A forced knockdown on every crossfire, more than one pin shot per hold, a second helper hit on the same hold: each pushes the 24-damage cap and the P14-01 pace.
- A "counter that hits both attackers" as a separate move: the shove on escape is the small form; a damaging one would reward the victim for being held.

#### Balance and what is measured (for P18-24)

- Expected size of the effect: a pin shot happens at most once per hold and a hold is 0.3 to 1.4 per crowd fight (P18-25's table), so about 5 hp per fight against 100+ health; a crossfire adds about 1.7 hp per occurrence. That is inside the noise of 100 seeded fights (+-10 points), so the targets are checked on both sides of the switch. Per-hit numbers (10, 8 stamina, 240 / 300 / 180 locks, 1.25, 24 ticks, 100 degrees) are starting values.
- Reference with `BREAKPOINT.simulate` (n = 100 per row, seats swapped, `teamAttacks` On and Off on the same seeds): 2v2 Normal, Hard and Expert, 3v3 Hard, 1v3 and 1v5 Hard (AI player), and the P18-21 goon stage 1 / 3 / 5 / 6 rows with and without an ally. Targets: (a) the P14-01 style-pair rates (136 pairs) and every recorded 1v1 hash stay bit for bit; (b) team lineups stay at 45 to 55 percent for equal teams and move at most 5 points between On and Off; (c) brawl clear rates stay inside the P14-01 / P18-20 bands (Easy 85 or more, Normal 50 to 70, Hard 25 to 45, Expert 10 to 25 for main-fighter groups; the goon table's rates for goons) and move at most 5 points on Normal and above; (d) pin shots per fight at most 1 for a team of two, at most 2 for a crowd, per person at most 1 in 5 s; (e) fight length moves at most 2 s. If a bound fails, lower in this order: `ASSIST_DMG` 10 to 8, `CROSSFIRE_MULT` 1.25 to 1.15, then the locks; never the escape window.
- Raising the CPU's pressure on a person (Easy has no enemy pin shot at all by the token rule; Normal and Hard at most one helper) is intended: P18-21's goon factors already scale goon damage (x0.45 of a main fighter at Normal), and `assistHit` takes the goon's damage stat, so a goon kick is about 4 to 5 damage.

Eligibility table: a free teammate within reach turns a Grapple press into a pin shot; out of reach, not carrying, lack of stamina, cooldown, victim lock, a hold younger than `escapeStartFor(victim)` (tick 11 and 13 rear), same-team victim, free-for-all, `teamAttacks` off, victim not in `S.CLINCH`: each stays a plain grab.
  2. The hit: one hit exactly, the damage formula with the stats and the combo scale, the stamina drain, the 6 stamina floor, the victim stays `S.CLINCH`, the credit and momentum go to the helper, a KO ends the hold.
  3. Once per hold, the helper cooldown 240, the victim lock 300, a second helper on the same hold: when both go active on one tick `apply` lets the first in the alternating start order (`tick % count`) land and makes the later one a whiff; when it goes active later `assisted` is already set and it is a whiff. A press at hold tick 11 stays a plain grab and at tick 12 (rear grip: 13 stays, 14 is a pin shot) starts a pin shot.
  4. Whiff and cancel: victim escaped, thrown or released before the active frames finds nobody; a hit on the helper in its startup cancels it; nothing else (a normal strike, a thrown item, a flying body) can hit a held fighter.

Owner device checks for P16-03 (the coordinator adds): hold an enemy in a 2v2 and watch the ally kick (touch, pad, keyboard); get pinned by two goons in Arcade and see whether the escape reads; flank an enemy with the ally and look for CROSSFIRE.

The file is 1,178,607 bytes today (LF + BOM), so the budget of 4,000,000 is not a limit; the design reuses `clinchStrike`'s formula, the attack-state machinery and the AI's walk code instead of copying them.

#### What the owner can change

Each is one number or one line:
- Whether CPU enemies may team-attack a person at all (today yes, gated by tokens; "no" is `teamAttacks` forced off for enemy helpers).
- Pin shot damage 10 and stamina 8, the helper cooldown 240, the victim lock 300, the one-per-hold cap.
- The escape: window unchanged today; a later window (for example +4 ticks while a helper is in reach) or a harsher or softer stamina floor.
- Crossfire factor 1.25, window 24 ticks, angle 100 degrees, lock 180, or removing Crossfire.
- The Free Fight row (default On; or no row and always on).
- Rescue by hitting the holder, the toss-and-catch throw, a damaging shove on escape (all rejected for now).
- The AI's join chances (0.3 / 0.55 / 0.8 / 1.0) and the holder's wait (32 ticks).

### P18-26 mobile release recommendation (2026-11-07)

From the research in Appendix B (P18-26). Costs and fees as read on 2026-11-07; re-read before pricing.

Recommended path in 3 steps:
1. **Now to the device checks (cost 0):** ship the single file to itch.io, free or pay-what-you-want from 0, "Mobile Friendly" on; tell phone players to use Add to Home Screen. Do P16-01/02/04 and the owner device test (P16-03), and add a save export/import before anyone relies on saves. If the owner allows GitHub Pages, add a manifest and service worker (two small files) for a real installable, offline PWA.
2. **Android store first (25 USD once):** wrap with Capacitor (no hosting needed) or TWA if Pages is on; use friends and family as the 12 closed testers for 14 days; free download, price model D1 (cosmetic supporter pack) or D2 (one-time unlock about 3-5 EUR), through Play Billing with a feature-detected bridge; no ads. Needs a DECIDE on the bridge against the "no external dependencies" rule (it lives outside the game file).
3. **iPhone store only after Android/itch.io show players (99 USD per year):** same Capacitor project built through a cloud Mac service, offline-first, native touches to pass 4.2, Apple IAP for the same unlock, Small Business 15% rate. Until then iPhone stays on Add to Home Screen. Re-read Google's new fee table and Apple's standard rate before setting the price.

Open questions for the owner: enable GitHub Pages (public); allow two extra files for PWA offline; pick D1, D2 or D3; accept a native billing bridge outside the game file.

### P18-27 accessibility as identity decided (2026-11-07)

- Friend (2026-11-02, Appendix B): "if it can establish its own identity ... perhaps with a more accessible approach compared to games like Tekken, I think there could be potential." Owner (2026-11-02): the game stays 3D. The owner delegated design choices ("select the correct option") and raised the size budget to 4,000,000 LF bytes on 2026-11-07, so size is not the deciding limit here. Decided by the coordinator's delegate; every "Decided" line can be changed by the owner. Nothing here changes the game code; P18-14 (X-factor) reads "Inputs for P18-14" at the end.
- What the game already has (base 8aa8c39, `breakpoint.html` line numbers):
  - Settings (`SETTING_DEFS` 593): **Auto-assist** (610, bool, default Off; string window x2 = `ASSIST_STRING_WINDOW` 1032, a string goes on after a whiff, `pickString` 5804; read from the setting for human input only, 1338, so the CPU and the dummy never get it); **Reduced motion** (600, also set from the operating system's preference; turns Flashes and Rumble to Reduced and Strike trails Off, `REDUCED_MOTION_ROWS` 618; it also damps camera motion, idle sway and story spins, 2575, 4205, 6372, 11500); Flashes (601), Controller rumble (602), Strike trails (603), High-contrast HUD (604), Camera shake (598), UI scale (599, 0.8 to 1.5), Movement directions (597), Touch controls auto/on/off (609), Story scenes full/short/off and Auto-advance (614, 615).
  - Difficulty: four levels (`DIFFICULTY` 8418; Easy reacts 20 ticks late, hits at x0.75, `blockSkill` 0.15, so it rarely blocks), one Difficulty row on the first screen of Arcade, Survival, Free Fight and Tournament (`levelRow` 13839), saved per mode; a new save starts on Easy in every mode (`Game.selection` 11926).
  - Training: dummy modes (`DUMMY_MODES` 9360: stand, block high/low, crouch, jump, walk, attack high/low/mixed, block after first hit, CPU Easy to Expert), infinite health and stamina toggles (9829, 14414), six scenarios (`SCENARIOS` 13239; the sixth practises holds), the defence reading PERFECT / EARLY n / LATE n (`defenceReading` 9366), the LINK and DEFEND frame lines, hold practice text (14924). It is reached from the pause menu of Training and from the main menu.
  - Help screens: the Move list per fighter (14231 to 14258: signature moves, frame data, `DEFENSE_HELP` 5025, `COMBO_HELP` 5029, "Chain before a move is 60% recovered"), the Controls screen, the per-input controls card (`controlsCardHtml` 13373: move, Punch, Kick, Defend with the fighter's own defence, Grab, Jump/Crouch, one line on strings; shown once per input type keyboard / gamepad / touch, `seenControls` in Progress 946, 962, closes itself after `ONBOARD_MS` 8 s).
  - Tips shown once: the controls card per input type; the first clinch (`firstClinchTip` 14790, `seenClinch`), the first hold (`firstHoldTip` 14802, `seenHold`), the browser-shortcut toast (13474, per session); `LOW STAMINA` banner (335, shown by the HUD every time the tank is low, not once).
  - Touch: nine buttons (`TOUCH_BUTTONS` 13179: PUNCH, KICK, DEFEND, GRAB large/medium, JUMP, DUCK, pause, and context USE / LOCK that only appear when useful, 13180); crouch by holding the stick down (18 ticks, `TOUCH_DUCK_TICKS` 1028; P17-19), run by two flicks (`TOUCH_RUN_TICKS` 1027), a sidestep flick; gamepad and keyboard labels in `GAMEPAD_LABELS` / `keyName` (13176, 13362).
  - Not there: any guided first fight, any on-screen explanation of stamina, stun or the high/low guard before the player meets it, an assist for guarding, a "start here" in the Move list, a prompt after repeated losses.
- What a new player must learn today before a first win (counted from the code; the first four are what a win needs, the rest can wait):

  | # | Thing | Needed for a first win? | How it is taught today |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 1 | Move, and the camera-relative stick (Movement directions) | yes | controls card (once) |
  | 2 | Punch and Kick, and chaining: press again as a hit lands, within the string window (`ATTACK_STRING_TICKS`); some strings need Duck held | yes (a jab alone wins Easy) | one line on the card; Move list |
  | 3 | Defend: **Block** (hold) or **Sway** (tap just before the hit, 0 to 6 ticks is perfect) depends on the fighter's style; Duck + Defend for low | yes (Easy still lands hits; blocking halves the loss) | card names the fighter's own defence; Move list |
  | 4 | Stamina: every move costs, an empty tank hits at x0.6 and starts slowly, a run or a sway needs some | yes | LOW STAMINA banner when it is already low |
  | 5 | Stun: you cannot act while hit, a chain cannot be stopped, a guard held through it starts the moment you are free (combo break) | no (it is why you lose, not how you win) | `COMBO_HELP` in the Move list only |
  | 6 | Grab, throw, escape, clinch, hold, tackle | no | grab hint when alone with a foe; clinch and hold tips once |
  | 7 | High / mid / low and which move hits what | no on Easy, yes from Normal | frame-data lines in Move list and Training |
  | 8 | Jump, sidestep, run, items (USE / LOCK), walls and ring-out | no | card (jump), item hints |
  | 9 | 32 fighters with 16 different styles: which to pick | no | Move list per fighter, the creator |

  A new Tekken player faces about 100 moves per fighter and frame data for all of them; here the same entry costs 4 ideas and then 5 optional layers, so the gap is already smaller. What is missing is that the game does not say which ideas matter first, and does not explain 4 and 5 until the player has lost to them.
- Comparison (sources, URLs, dates read and verified marks: Appendix B entry "P18-27 - How fighters ease new players in (researched 2026-11-07)", file `P18-27B.md`; own words; claims no source confirmed were dropped, the list is at the end of that entry):
  - Street Fighter 6 has a second control scheme (Modern, a four-button layout where a special move is one button plus a direction), is the default on first launch and can be switched to Classic in the settings; press reports a price, about 20% less damage on specials done with Modern's one-button shortcut (Capcom's wording not found; verified partly). Lesson taken: the on-ramp is a choice the player can leave later, with the same fight rules underneath, and it carries a price so skill still pays.
  - Tekken 8 has Special Style (one button per recommended move or combo, switched on or off at any point of a match with one button; the auto-combos are not optimal, so strong players still do it by hand; verified partly) and Arcade Quest (avatar, a mentor, demos then practice, then fights against the computer; reviews are mixed: some praise the teaching, others call it a slog or too heavy on tutorial; verified partly). Lessons taken: teach inside play, keep the lines short and shown once, keep the assist a switch and its ceiling low on purpose (it must never be better than skill), and do not make it a mode.
  - Super Smash Bros. (one normal and one special button, a held direction picks the move) and Fantasy Strike (stick plus three buttons, no motion inputs, made easy for everyone, not as a mode; reviews praise it and some say it is thin) show that a small button set can carry a big move list. Lesson taken: our four buttons are enough, and the learning cost is in the layers, which the tips and "Start here" order. Too little depth reads as shallow, so the depth layers stay.
  - Tekken 2 onward guards high and mid for you while you stand and retreat (Appendix B, P1-01, Tekken, neutral guard, REFERENCE line 301), and crouching guards low: the high/low rule is learned by being hit. Lesson taken: our Duck + Defend is the same two-button chore, which is worse on a phone.
  - Our own reading, not a source: Arcade on Easy is already the first-fight guide; it only lacks narration.
- Decided: **"Easy to enter, deep to master" in four parts, none of which is a new mode, a new screen or a new on-screen button.** The first fight is taught by short coaching lines at the moment the player meets each thing (shown once, saved), a second assist makes guarding one gesture, the Move list opens with a "Start here" block, and the game offers help after repeated losses. Defaults for a new save stay as they are (Easy everywhere, Auto-assist Off). Nothing in the simulation changes for anyone who leaves the new switch Off, so every recorded fingerprint and the P14-01 balance are untouched.

  | # | Part | Decided | Because |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 1 | **Coaching lines** (the "first-fight guide") | A table `COACH_TIPS` of 10 one-line tips, each tied to an event the game already emits; a tip shows once, ever (`Progress.d.tips`, a small object of booleans read through the cleaner like `seenClinch`), on the existing hint strip (the one the grapple hint uses, `showHint` defined at 14783, called at 14687, not a modal and not a new element), for 4 s, never during the countdown, a replay, a Versus seat 2, the benchmark or when the controls card is open; at most one per round; none at all after the player's 20th fight (the fight count is `wins + losses`). The list is in "The tips" below | Teaches at the moment of need, as Arcade Quest does, without a tutorial mode; the show-once rule is kept; one table holds text, trigger and key, so a tip cannot exist in the code and not in the tests |
  | 2 | **Guard assist** (new setting, default Off) | `SETTING_DEFS.guardAssist` bool, label "Guard assist", hint "Defend alone guards high and low for you (no Duck needed). The CPU does not get it. Perfect blocks still need good timing, and a guard that has to switch height is never perfect." Human input only, exactly like Auto-assist (`it.assist` 1338 gets a sibling `it.guardAssist`). Rule: while Defend is held and the player is standing or ducking, a strike that would be blocked only at the other height is blocked anyway, as a plain block (no perfect, no counter, no combo break from that block); everything else about the guard (stamina cost, the front half-plane, the 30-tick perfect cooldown) is unchanged. Sway fighters: a tap sways away from either height (already true) so the setting changes nothing for them. Auto-assist keeps its row and its meaning. | Duck + Defend is two inputs held together; on a phone it is the stick-down hold (18 ticks, P17-19) plus a thumb on DEFEND, which new players do not manage. A one-gesture guard is Tekken's neutral guard with our button; it removes the high/low guess without removing timing or stamina, so skill still beats it (perfect block, sway, grabs and throws ignore it) |
  | 3 | **Start here** in the Move list | A block above the signature moves: "Start here: 1 Punch, Punch, Punch = your first string; 2 hold Defend when the foe starts a move; 3 Grab when the foe is guarding; 4 stop hitting when the stamina bar is low." The first string and the best-known three moves of the fighter are marked with a star in the list (a `first` flag on three entries of each style's `signature`, or the first row of the style's string table: no new data if the first row is used). Plain words, touch labels and key names by input type (the Move list already does this) | The Move list is where a stuck player goes; today it opens with data, the thing a beginner does not need |
  | 4 | **Help after losses** | One tip (a coach tip, once): after the second loss in a row in the first 10 fights, a toast "Hard fight? Settings has Auto-assist and Guard assist, and Training shows every move." with no button (tap anywhere closes it). No dynamic difficulty: the CPU level never changes by itself (it would hide Easy from the player and break replay and the P14-01 ladders) | Offers the lever at the moment it matters, without deciding for the player |

- The tips (text is plain, ASCII, uses the key names of the player's device through `keyName`; trigger = an existing event; key = field in `Progress.d.tips`; all once only):

  | Key | Trigger | Line (max 70 characters) |
  |---|---|---|
  | `punch` | the first fight ends round 1 without the player having thrown a second Punch within a string window, after 15 s of fight | "Press PUNCH again as a hit lands to chain a string." |
  | `stam` | the first time stamina drops under 30% | "Strikes cost stamina. Stop attacking for a moment and it fills again." (the existing LOW STAMINA banner still shows) |
  | `block` | the first block (any) | "Blocked. Strong moves break a block unless it is perfect." |
  | `perfect` | the first perfect block or sway | "PERFECT! That breaks a combo." |
  | `low` | the first time the player is hit by a low move while not ducking, in the first 5 fights | "That was low. Hold DUCK with DEFEND to guard low." (Guard assist On: not shown) |
  | `stun` | the third consecutive hit on the player (combo) | "While you are hit you cannot act. Hold DEFEND to guard the moment you are free." |
  | `down` | the first knockdown of the player | "Press DEFEND on the ground to get up quickly." |
  | `grab` | the first time the player is grabbed (a grab or throw) while holding Defend | "Guards do not stop a grab. Move away, or tap GRAB to escape." |
  | `item` | the first time the player stands within reach of a lying item | "USE picks it up. Hit with it, or throw it." |
  | `lose` | part 4 above | see part 4 |

  The existing controls card, clinch tip and hold tip stay as they are. The ten keys add up to under 700 characters of text. Tips are plain text on a strip and never flash, so Reduced motion does not hide them (it only turns off the strip's fade). Tips are never shown for the P2 of Versus or co-op seats 2 to 4 (the first seat of a human gets them), and `Progress.d.tips` is saved once per tip, not per input type (a player who learns on a phone does not see the same line on a keyboard).
- Rejected: **a separate tutorial mode or forced first fight** (an extra mode, extra save state, and the show-once rule says teaching lives in play; a forced screen is what makes people quit before a first fight). **Dynamic difficulty** (the sim stays the same for all; see part 4). **A third control scheme** (Modern-style one-button specials: the game has 4 buttons and 16 styles, a scheme would need its own move table per style, about 3 to 5 KB per style and a new balance pass; Auto-assist plus Guard assist already cover the same ground). **A fixed "easy mode" with damage reduction** (the Difficulty row is it). **A new on-screen button** (nothing needs one: Guard assist removes the need for the DUCK + DEFEND chord, and the tips use the existing strip). **Turning Auto-assist on by default** (it changes how strings feel for everyone who just wants to play; the first-loss offer is better, and a veteran does not have to find an off switch). **Showing frame data to beginners** (stays in Training and the Move list).
- Touch, gamepad, keyboard: nothing new to press; Guard assist is a setting (works on all three, since it is read from the same Defend intent); tips name the control of the device used last (`keyName`, 13362). On the 390x844 and 844x390 phones the strip is the one the grapple hint already uses, so no layout work; the longest line is 70 characters at the small hint size, which fits two lines at 390 px.
- Determinism, replay, online and balance (P14-01): the simulation reads `Settings.v.autoAssist` once per human intent (1338) and does not read it anywhere else; Guard assist follows the same path (a field of the intent), so with it Off nothing changes in any run. With it On the input stream is the same; the only change is which strikes a held Defend blocks. For replay and online it must be a per-seat `cfg` field (`cfg.assist` bit mask for strings and guard per seat), not a viewer setting read inside the sim; today Auto-assist is read from `Settings` at the human intent, so P18-19's single `cfg` builder or the online task must copy both into `cfg`. The build task below adds the `cfg` fields, reads them in the intent step for human seats and keeps the Settings as the source for local play. Balance: P14-01 ladders and the Block-vs-Sway 45 to 55 % split are measured with the AI as the player and neither assist on, so they do not move; one extra measurement (below) checks the assist does not beat Hard.
- Performance: coach tips run on events and once per round, so no per-tick cost; `Progress.d.tips` is one small object; Guard assist adds one comparison in the block test of a player with the flag.
- Edge cases:

  | Case | Result |
  |---|---|
  | Guard assist On, a Block fighter, a mid strike while ducked | blocked as a plain block (the height is ignored) |
  | Guard assist On and a perfect-timed press against a low move while standing | perfect rules unchanged: a stand guard against a low move is a plain block, never perfect, so the timing skill is still the way to a break |
  | Guard assist On, Sway fighter | no change (a sway already dodges both) |
  | Guard assist On in Versus | per seat; P2 has its own switch via the seat's own setting; both shown on the Versus card line |
  | A throw, grab, tackle or thrown body at a guard | not blocked at all, as today |
  | Tips and Reduced motion / High-contrast | the strip uses the HUD text colour; no flash, no animation beyond the existing fade (off under Reduced motion) |
  | A tip fires in the same tick as a story scene or the controls card | the card wins; the tip waits for the next round (the key is not set until it is shown) |
  | A new save reaches a fight on a different device | the tips are per player, not per device; the controls card stays per input type |
  | The player turns Auto-assist or Guard assist off after the loss offer | nothing nags: the `lose` key is set |
  | Old save without `tips` | all false; players with many fights (`wins + losses` over 20) get none |
- Bytes (LF, estimated; the file is 1,178,607 bytes (LF) at 8aa8c39 and the budget is 4,000,000, so all of this fits twice over; the estimates are for the task's own cap):

  | Part | Bytes |
  |---|---|
  | `COACH_TIPS` table (10 lines, keys, triggers) | 1,500 |
  | `Coach` helper (show once, suppress rules, event hooks into `Events.on`), save field and cleaner | 1,100 |
  | Guard assist: setting + hint, intent flag, block-height rule, `cfg` field for replay | 900 |
  | Move list "Start here" block and the star marks | 700 |
  | Loss offer | 350 |
  | **Total** | **about 4,550**; cap for the task 5,500 |

  Fallbacks if the measured size is over the cap, in this order: shorter tip lines (about 300 bytes); drop the `item` and `grab` tips (about 350, they are the least needed for a first win); drop the stars in the Move list (about 150). None of the four parts is dropped without asking the owner.
- Self-tests the build must add (names start `Accessibility (P18-27):`; none may skip, weaken or delete an older test):
  1. the tip table: each key fires once on its trigger with a human in seat 1, never twice in the same session or after a reload (read back through a fresh `Store`), never for a CPU, seat 2, the benchmark, a replay or a countdown, at most one per round, none after 20 fights;
  2. text: every line is at most 70 characters, plain ASCII, passes the P17-05 design-note scan, and names the control of the device used last (touch names DUCK / DEFEND, gamepad names R1, keyboard the bound key);
  3. Guard assist: standing with Defend held blocks a low move as plain, ducked blocks a mid move as plain, never perfect on a height switch, a CPU never gets it, Off changes nothing (a seeded 1v1 hash with the flag Off equals the recorded one), a Sway fighter unchanged, grabs and tackles still not blocked;
  4. replay: the same input log with the `cfg` flags Off, On and On through JSON round-trip gives the Off, On and On hashes; `Settings` changed mid-fight changes nothing;
  5. save: `Progress.d.tips` cleaned (missing, wrong type, extra key), an old save loads with all false;
  6. Move list "Start here" shows the device's key names and the star marks the same three moves as the Training panel's signature list;
  7. the loss offer shows after the second loss in a row inside 10 fights, once;
  8. layout at 390x844 and 844x390 (strip does not cover the stamina bar or the buttons; two lines fit), in the browser run;
  9. balance run (below), recorded in the log.
- Balance check the build runs and records (method of P0-06 / `BREAKPOINT.simulate`, 12 seeds per cell): the P18-33 Press script in a variant that never ducks (so it only has the standing guard), with Guard assist On against Off, and the normal Press script (which picks the right guard height, `it.crouch = tr.kind === 'block' && tr.h === 'L'`, 8993 and 9277) as the ceiling; each against Easy, Normal, Hard and Expert. The AI picks the right height when it reacts, so a plain AI-as-human run would hardly show the assist. The aim: Guard assist On moves the never-ducks variant's win rate by at most 15 points at Easy and Normal and by at most 8 at Hard and Expert, and never takes it above the normal Press script (the ceiling), so the assist makes up for a missing duck and adds nothing beyond right-height play. If it moves more, narrow the rule (for example, plain blocks only from the second hit of a string), not the CPU numbers.
- Open (for the owner; each is decided above and can be changed): (1) Guard assist is a second switch, not a value of Auto-assist (a saved bool keeps its meaning). The alternative is one "Assist" row with Off / Strings / Strings + Guard, which saves one row (about 120 bytes) and one tap but needs a migration of the saved bool. (2) Assist is not marked in grades (there is no ranking to protect; the owner can add a small "ASSIST" tag in the result card). (3) Tips stop after 20 fights; the limit is a constant. (4) No tutorial mode; if the owner wants a guided first fight in Arcade, the cheapest version is a "stage 0" Training scenario using the six existing scenarios with the coach lines on (about 1,500 bytes), not a new mode.
- Inputs for P18-14 (X-factor):
  - Accessibility is the first half of the game's identity; the X-factor should be a feature that gives depth to players who stay: something that a new player can use at once (one gesture) and an expert can play with. Candidates from this entry: (a) **the perfect-timing layer** (0 to 6 ticks, Block and Sway, combo break) is already unlike other 3D fighters, because it is the same window for both defences and it is one button; it can be the signature if the cues are good (P18-04) and the tips teach it (`perfect` tip); (b) **the environment** (breakables, hazards, ring-out, raised ground, items) is a thing Tekken only has in a small amount, and it is easy to understand on a phone (a tip per hazard family could follow the `item` tip); (c) **a comeback mechanic** in the spirit of Tekken 8's Heat or Tekken 6's Rage would suit this audience (a trailing player gets a short buff), but any such mechanic must be explained by one coach line and be inactive for a new player's first two fights, and it needs a balance run like the Guard assist one.
  - Constraints the X-factor must keep: no new on-screen button; every new idea gets one coach line and a Training line; nothing that makes a first fight harder to read; anything numeric goes through `cfg`, not Settings, so replay and online hold.
  - A design rule to carry: "a new idea costs one line the player sees once, or it does not ship".
- Build notes for the implementing task (task **BP-P18-48 "Implement P18-27 accessibility"**, created by the coordinator in the tasklist with depends_on BP-P18-27; run it after P18-19 (the `cfg` builder) and P18-43; one batch, Sonnet implementer then Opus reviewer):
  - Order of work: (a) `COACH_TIPS` table and `Coach` (one source for text, trigger, key); the `tips` field in `Progress.fresh` (946) and its cleaner (962), reusing the `seenClinch` pattern; (b) hooks: use `Events.on` where the game already listens (13289, 13292); add the few events not emitted yet (first block, first knockdown of seat 1, stamina under 30%) as read-only events; (c) the strip: reuse `showHint` (defined 14783); (d) Guard assist: `SETTING_DEFS.guardAssist`, the intent flag next to `it.assist` (1338), the block-height test in `Combat.evaluate` (6966 to 6969: `S.BLOCK_H` blocks H and M, `S.BLOCK_L` blocks L; the search words `blockHigh` / `blockLow` only find key bindings), the `cfg.assist` field filled by the single `cfg` builder and read by `Fighter` for the human seats; (e) Move list block (14231); (f) the loss offer on the `matchEnd` event (11331 emits it for every mode; `onMatchEnd` 12546 is only the Tournament's handler, so do not put the offer there); (g) tests; (h) the balance run.
  - Traps: the assist must be read from `cfg` inside the sim, not from `Settings` (online and replay); with the flag Off every recorded hash must match; a tip trigger must never call anything that touches the sim state (read-only events only); do not set a tip key until the tip is actually shown (a suppressed tip comes back); `Progress.save` writes once per tip (the same as `seenClinch`); the Move list star must read the data (first string row), not a second list.
  - Docs: update the Settings hint list, the Move list help text and Appendix C in the same change; the P16-03 owner device list gets: on a phone, play the first fight at Easy with the tips On and read each line once; turn Guard assist On and block a low move without Duck; turn it Off again.
  - Checks: the node one-liner for size (cap 5,500 bytes over the base), the full browser self-test (the count must grow by the new tests), P0-06 reduced rows unchanged with the assist Off.
- Checks done for this entry: reading only (`breakpoint.html` at 8aa8c39, the tasklist, SPEC, Appendix B and the P18-42 entry); web research on 2026-11-07 for how Street Fighter 6 Modern controls, Tekken 8's Special Style and Arcade Quest, Smash and Fantasy Strike lower the entry barrier (written up with URLs, dates and verified marks in `P18-27B.md`, Appendix B; unsourced claims were dropped). Line numbers and the file size re-checked against 8aa8c39. No game file, test file or fingerprint was touched, and no test was run.

### P18-48 built: accessibility as identity (the P18-27 decision)

- Built as decided, none of it a mode, screen or on-screen button. (1) **Coaching lines**: `COACH_TIPS` (10 keys, one table of key and text) and `Coach` next to `Progress`; `Progress.d.tips` is an object of booleans, cleaned like `seenClinch` (missing, wrong type or extra key reads as not shown). The events that ask for a line are read-only listeners (`Coach.hook`); a line waits as `pending` and its key is saved only when `Coach.line` puts it on the grapple hint strip (`hudUpdate`, after the clinch and hold hints), for 240 ticks, at most one per round, only for a person on seat 1 in the fight phase, never in Training, a benchmark or replay (`cfg.benchmark` / `cfg.replay`), a crowd of several people, with the controls card open, or after 20 fights. (2) **Guard assist** (`SETTING_DEFS.guardAssist`, Off by default, after Auto-assist): `Combat.evaluate` blocks the other height as a plain block while a guard is up (`switched`: never perfect); grabs, throws, a Sway fighter and the CPU are untouched. (3) **Start here** block (the first string is read from the fighter's own table: three presses, twice or once, Kick when a crate is carried; a review fix) and `*` marks (signature moves of the style, from `style.signature`, in the Data cell because the name cell is parsed by the Move list test) in the Move list; one sentence about Guard assist in About and Help. (4) **Loss offer**: `Coach.matchEnd` (a listener on `matchEnd`), second loss in a row, first 10 fights, once, not when both assists are already on, as a toast of 6 s.
- `cfg.assist` (bit 1 = Auto-assist strings, bit 2 = Guard assist) is copied from Settings by `Game.beginMatch` (a rematch re-reads it) and read by `MatchSim.readAssist` for human seats only, so a replay or an online seat does not read the viewer's Settings. A match with no `cfg.assist` (a test, the simulator) has no assist at all: the sim never reads Settings (review fix). One mask covers every human seat; a future online or replay task must turn it into a per-seat mask. `'assist'` joins the keys the Free Fight merge test ignores when it compares `Game.config`, as `items` and `hazards` already were.
- Differences from the decision, all small: the `stam` line comes from the existing low-stamina event (under 25 %, the LOW STAMINA banner) instead of a new 30 % event; the `stun`, `grab`, `block`, `stam` and loss lines are shorter than the decision's text (the stun line was 79 characters, the limit is 70); the loss toast closes by itself (no tap handler); only the signature moves are starred (the first string is named in Start here); Guard assist is one setting for every human seat, so the Versus card line is unchanged; the layout check at 390x844 and 844x390 is a browser check (not run here).
- Size (LF bytes): breakpoint.html 1,178,914 to 1,186,047 (+7,133). The decision's cap was 5,500 (estimate 4,550): over by 1,633; the total budget is 4,000,000. Fallbacks left, in the decision's order: drop the `item` and `grab` lines (about 450 bytes), drop the stars (about 150); the rest of the overage is the Coach code (about 3,300, the decision estimated 1,100 for the helper) and comments.
- Tests (11, names start `Accessibility (P18-27):`): the tip table (each key fires once on its event, shows 4 s, one per round, saved when shown, kept after a reload); suppression (CPU, seat 2, benchmark, replay, countdown, Training, open card, 20 fights; a held-back line is not used up); text (ASCII, 70 characters, no design notes, the device's names); Progress cleaning; Guard assist rules (both heights, perfect, grab, Sway, CPU); the three recorded 1v1 fingerprints with the bits 0 and 3; replay (same log, JSON round trip, Settings changed mid-fight; On differs from Off; strings from the config); `beginMatch` and rematch copy; Move list (Start here in the three devices' names, stars equal the signature list of all 16 styles); the loss offer. Checked with mutants (perfect allowed on a height switch, Settings read in the sim, no phase gate, the CPU seat reading the flag, a key saved before it is shown): each fails a test. The self-test count went from 607 to 618 in the headless run. Review fixes: the tip strip is `width:max-content` with `max-width:min(92%,26em)` and sits at 34 % from the top in portrait (away from the stick and buttons); the layout test for it is a browser check, left to P16-03 (it needs the touch controls and a real layout, and no browser was run); both assist hints end with "From the next match."
- Balance (headless harness, a scratch script not kept in the repo): the P18-33 player-like script as KAI against MARA (CPU damage levels, no items or hazards), 12 seeds on both start sides (24 matches per cell; Hard and Expert also seeds 13 to 48, 72 more), wins of the script. The variant that never ducks with Guard assist Off / On, and the normal script (ducks to the height it sees) as the ceiling:

  | Level | Never ducks, Off | Never ducks, On | Ducks (ceiling) | On minus Off |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | Easy | 24 / 24 | 24 / 24 | 24 / 24 | 0 points |
  | Normal | 24 / 24 | 24 / 24 | 24 / 24 | 0 points |
  | Hard | 77 / 96 (80.2 %) | 70 / 96 (72.9 %) | 69 / 96 (71.9 %) | -7.3 points |
  | Expert | 32 / 96 (33.3 %) | 28 / 96 (29.2 %) | 30 / 96 (31.3 %) | -4.2 points |

  The limits (15 points at Easy and Normal, 8 at Hard and Expert, never above the ceiling) hold. Easy and Normal are full (the script wins every match), so the assist cannot show there; at Hard and Expert the assist does not raise the win rate (it lowers it a little, since the guard spends stamina), and it sits within one match of the ceiling. The first 24-match Hard cell read 19 / 20 / 19 and Expert 11 / 12 / 14: single cells of 24 move by a few matches, the 96-match cells are the ones to read. The Press-script rows of P0-06 and the three 1v1 fingerprints are unchanged with the assists Off.

### P18-14 X-factor recommended (2026-11-07)

- Owner (2026-11-01, Appendix A, REFERENCE line 186): "The main thing I feel is currently missing is an X-factor: one genuinely unique feature that gives the game its own identity. Something memorable that makes it stand out from other games in the genre." The same writer (line 180 to 182) likes the new levels and "the interaction with objects in the environment" and wants it "developed further". Task rule: the owner picks from the options; the coordinator gives a recommended one. So this entry is a **recommendation, not the pick**: BP-P18-49 below is written for the recommendation and starts only after the owner's OK (human_intervention of BP-P18-14). If the owner picks another option, the row is swapped, not stacked. BP-P18-14 is not ticked until the owner picks; the coordinator sets `tracking.human_intervention.required` to true with this entry as the resume point. Written by the coordinator's delegate under the standing "select the correct option" go, which does not cover this pick (TASKLIST line 3071 put it back to the owner). Nothing here changes the game code, a test or a fingerprint. Base: `main` at 2041038, `breakpoint.html` 1,178,914 bytes (LF, BOM counted) of 4,000,000; line numbers below are of that commit and move when P18-13, P18-48 and P18-45 land.
- Research: Appendix B, "P18-14 - What the closest games do for identity (researched 2026-11-07)" (file `P18-14B.md`; URLs, dates read and verified marks there; claims no page confirmed were dropped, the list is at its end). Read there: Dead or Alive (Danger Zones), Def Jam: Fight for NY (environment, crowd, momentum), Injustice and Mortal Kombat X (interactive objects), Smash (18 stage-hazard kinds), Tekken 8 (Heat, stage destruction, Super Ghost Battle), Smash Figure Players, Virtua Fighter 4 Evolution, Street Fighter III parry, Garou Just Defend, Sifu (structure, aging), Grand Theft Auto (wanted level), Shadow Fight 2. P18-27's entry (Appendix B, "P18-27 - How fighters ease new players in") is option A.
- What the sources say about the genre, in short (own words; marks as in Appendix B):
  - Scenery that hurts is the genre's normal form of "environment": Dead or Alive's Danger Zones (extra damage; falls, explosive and breakable walls, moving obstacles), Def Jam's walls, gates and crowd, Injustice's per-character objects, Mortal Kombat's weapons from the scenery, Tekken 8's break-through walls and floors. Smash lists 18 hazard kinds and has a few one-step triggers (a switch, a trapdoor, a vehicle that explodes an item), and no general chain system. None of the six environment pages describes one scenery effect lighting, breaking or crushing another by a rule (not found in the part read; absence is not proof).
  - A comeback state is the other standard identity move (Tekken 8 Heat and Rage, Mortal Kombat's meter, Def Jam's Blazin' Moves, Garou's T.O.P.); here that is the Momentum gauge and the ultimate (P18-08), already planned.
  - A defence-timing reward is established in 2D (Street Fighter III parry, Garou Just Defend) and in the 3D brawler Sifu (parry, structure gauge). An AI that copies a player exists in Tekken 8 (Super Ghost Battle), Smash (Figure Players) and, as top-player styles, Virtua Fighter 4 Evolution. A police or heat clock is known from Grand Theft Auto; no fighting game with one was found. The nearest mobile fighter, Shadow Fight 2, is 2D, silhouette art, fantasy and energy-limited, so it does not compete on identity.
  - Sifu shows that one systemic hook that touches every fight (aging) is what reviewers remember a small brawler by.
- What the game already has that an X-factor can stand on (`breakpoint.html` at 2041038):
  - A rules matrix of nine scenery rules (P9, "System rules matrix", R1 to R9) that already chain by material: an arc runs through metal conductors (`Arena.linkConductors` 3508, `CHAIN_MAX` 6 at 2858, `hazardStart` 10538 damages them), a spark-sensitive material lights in an arc or fire zone (`MATERIALS.paper` and `.plastic` carry `spark: 1`, 2844 to 2853; `stepFire` 10648 to 10683 with `FIRE_MAX` 4 at 2859 and `FIRE_SPREAD_R` 1.0), fire spreads to near objects every `FIRE_SPREAD_TICKS` 60 (10678 to 10682), a burnt object breaks (`burnObject` 10695), a broken support drops what rests on it (`Arena.dropSupported` 3500), a collapsed deck crushes neighbours and the fighters under it (`stepCollapse` 10629, `CRUSH_OBJECTS` 4 "so a collapse can chain, deterministically", comment at 10638), a thrown or tipped barrel pools fire (`hazardArm` 10527, `HAZARDS.fire` 5600), an extinguisher puts fire out (`douse` 10705). Credit follows the cause: `h.by` on every hazard, `blazeFor(o).by` for a fire (10686), `hazardHit` 10759 names `by` only when `canHurt` allows (9946, which also excludes the fighter itself).
  - The CPU already lures into, waits at and walks out of those zones (`considerHazard`, `hazardLure`, `hazardBait`, `holdAtHazard`, `leaveHazard`, P18-12 text), so a chain started by anyone is lived with by everyone.
  - Events for every step (`hazardTrigger` 10534, `hazardStart` 10541, `objIgnite` 10687, `objBreak` 3464, `deckCreak` 10625, `hazardHit` 10774) with popup text (`popAt` 14615 and the listeners at 13294 to 13298), sound (13068 to 13077) and effects (12777 to 12784) already attached. No event says which effect caused which, and no counter says how long a chain ran.
  - Environment damage gives no momentum today (`hazardHit` 10759 to 10775 has no call to `Combat.momentum` 6927; every strike, throw, clinch strike and tackle has).
  - P18-12 (decided) adds 16 interactions, six of them chains (W1 warehouse stock, S2 subway bundle and scaffold, G2 garage tyres, C1 live fence, R1 rooftop air-conditioning units, P2 live cage) and a hydrant that cuts fire; BP-P18-13 builds them. P18-27 (decided) adds the Coach (once-only lines) and the saved `tips` field; BP-P18-48 builds it.

Verified yes for the games, partly for their numbers (P18-27) | about 4,550 bytes (cap 5,500), 1 batch; **already a task: BP-P18-48** | An on-ramp is not a thing people remember a game by; it is the front door, not the room |

A shared window for two defence types is not described by any page read; whether a 3D fighter does it is unknown | about 1,400 bytes, 1 batch (the cues are P18-04, done) | Not unclaimed; hard for a first-time player to read a 7-tick window; it rewards the already skilled |
