  | A Easy to enter | 2 | 5 | 5 | 2 | 1 | 5 | 5 | 25 |
  | B The Beat | 2 | 5 | 3 | 5 | 2 | 4 | 4 | 25 |
  | C Street Chain | 4 | 5 | 4 | 4 | 5 | 4 | 4 | 30 |
  | D Echo | 3 | 3 | 2 | 4 | 2 | 2 | 2 | 18 |
  | E Sirens | 4 | 3 | 3 | 2 | 4 | 4 | 2 | 22 |

- **Recommended: C, Street Chain, on top of A.** Reasons, in order: (1) the owner named the environment the part to develop (2026-11-01: "the interaction with objects in the environment ... another layer to the gameplay"), so it answers both of his points at once; (2) it is the one option whose core already exists and is invisible: nine rules chain scenery by material, and nobody can tell, because no effect says what caused it and nothing counts it; making it legible costs about 2.9 KB, against 4 KB for D and a new save format; (3) the pages read describe single-step scenery in other games and no rule-driven chain, so "the street fights back, one thing sets off the next" is a claim the game can make without copying anyone's names, characters or look; (4) a newcomer uses it with the controls they already have (strike or throw a metal item at a panel, knock a foe into a jet) and sees a result within seconds, and an expert plans routes, lures a foe into a zone and cuts a chain with the hydrant or the extinguisher; (5) it asks for nothing new from the simulation's random numbers, buttons or Settings. A stays as the front door (it is already BP-P18-48); C is the room behind it. D is the runner-up and stays a later extension (see Rejected); B stays what it is (P18-04 cues, the `perfect` coach tip) without being promoted.
- Honest limits of the claim: "unique" here means "not described by any of the six scenery pages read"; it is never to be written as "no game has it" in the game's text, store page or release notes (Appendix B, claims dropped). The identity line to use is the player-facing one: "Light the street. Watch it spread."

#### Street Chain, as decided for build

- Name in text and on screen: **CHAIN**. A link is a scenery effect whose cause is another scenery effect or a fighter's trigger, not the fighter's own hit. The chain's number N is the depth of its deepest link (the spark is 1); links of the same depth are siblings. One popup is shown per new depth per chain id, so a chain shows at most `CHAIN_SHOW_MAX` popups.
- The links (this table is the list of what counts; nothing else does). A cause is carried by one field `link` on the hazard or object (`{ id, by, depth }`, `id` from a per-match counter like `hazardSeq` 10464, never a random number) and by one variable `cause` that `MatchSim` sets around the four step functions that fire effects and clears afterwards:

  | # | Link | Where it happens (2041038) | Cause passed on by | Depth |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | 0 | **Spark**: a fighter sets a hazard off (strike, thrown item, knock) or breaks a glass wall | `hazardStrike` 10549, `hazardItem` 10559, `hazardKnocked` 10566, `hazardBreak` 10570: the first three via `hazardArm` 10527, and `hazardBreak` 10574 directly | `h.link = new link(by)` (by = the credited fighter, or null for a timer hazard) | 1 (never shown alone) |
  | 1 | **Arc**: the panel energises its conductors | `hazardStart` 10540 (loop over `h.chain`) | conductors get `o.link` = next(`h.link`). In `hazardEffects` (10718) a fighter of an arc hazard that is reached only through a conductor (10511, not inside `def.r`) is hit with that conductor's `o.link` (depth 2), passed to `hazardHit` as an argument | 2 |
  | 2 | **Ignite**: a fire or arc zone lights an object | `stepFire` 10664 to 10672 (the `hot` hazard), `ignite` 10684 | `o.link` = next(`hot.link`) | +1 |
  | 3 | **Spread**: a burning object lights a neighbour | `stepFire` 10678 to 10682 | `next.link` = next(`o.link`) | +1 |
  | 4 | **Fall**: a broken object drops what rests on it (supports, scaffold tiers, speakers) | `Arena.dropSupported` 3500, `breakDeck` 3470, the queue push at 3482 | the dropped piece and the collapse record carry `Arena.cause` | +1 |
  | 5 | **Crush**: a landed collapse breaks a neighbour or hurts a fighter | `stepCollapse` 10629 (neighbour loop 10639 to 10643, fighter loop 10634 to 10637) | `cause` = the record's link while the loop runs | +1 for each neighbour that breaks |
  | 6 | **Burn**: a fighter set alight in a linked zone | `hazardEffects` 10725 (`f.burnBy`), `stepFire` 10653 (`BURN_SRC.by`) | `f.burnLink = h.link` next to `f.burnBy`; `BURN_SRC.link = f.burnLink` at 10653, cleared after the call | same depth as the zone |
  | 7 | **Payoff**: a linked zone, a burn or a crush hurts a foe | `hazardHit` 10759 | reads `h.link` (and the crush source's) | not a link; a stat and momentum |

  A burnt object that simply burns out (`burnObject` 10695 then `Arena.breakObject` 3407) is not a link of its own: only what it drops or crushes is. A weak deck that gives way (`stepLoad` 10610), or any break whose cause is a fighter's own hit, starts no chain: its fall and crush carry `link: null`. The chain ends by itself; depth is capped at `CHAIN_SHOW_MAX` 9 for display only. A burning object keeps its link across rounds (10492 keeps its fire and credit), and `Arena.reset` (3354) rebuilds objects with `link: null`, so a new level state starts clean.
- What the player sees and hears (all existing channels, no new element): at depth 2 and above, each new depth of a chain shows one popup "CHAIN x2", "x3" ... at the place of the link that reached it (`popAt` 14615, the colour of the hazard warning '#ffb000' used at 13298), once per depth per chain id; a rising two-note motif (a `chain` entry next to `CUE_NOTES` 12731, volume as the existing hazard sounds, through `allow`); at depth 3 and above a small camera nudge through `Camera.impact` (2574, which Reduced motion already switches off). The popup is plain text and does not flash, so Flashes and Reduced motion need no new rule. A chain with `by` null (a timer hazard) is shown in the neutral '#d0d8e8' (the stage-name colour at 13295), counts for nobody.
- What it pays (one rule, no new number): damage a **linked** zone, conductor shock, burn or crush does to a foe counts for the fighter who lit the chain at the strike rate. In `hazardHit` (10759), when the hazard's link has a `by`, depth is 2 or more, `canHurt(by, f)` holds (so never the fighter itself, never a teammate with Friendly fire off) and the hit did damage, call `Combat.momentum(by, f, amount)` (6927), the same function and the same `MOMENTUM_PER_DAMAGE` 1.6 and 0.5 share as a strike. The street therefore pays like a punch, but only for a chain, not for a plain barrel or a plain panel (depth 1). A panel's 14 shock through a conductor (depth 2) is about 22 gauge points, and a linked fire zone's 4 about 6. For a crush hit the call also sets `f.lastFoe` to the lighter (6928), which moves later scenery credit; self-test 4 checks it. Both sides can earn it, and the CPU that stands in a zone it did not light pays the player, not itself.
- Counted and shown afterwards: per fighter `chains` (chains of depth 2 or more that fighter started), `chainMax` (the deepest) and `chainDmg` (damage from linked zones to foes), in `newStats` 9857; one line on the results card ("Chain: best 4, 31 damage", only when `chainMax >= 2`; the card code is at 14429 to 14490); `Progress.d.chainBest` (a number, cleaned like `arcadeBest`, `Progress.fresh` 946). **No change to `fightGrade` 924** (P14-01 targets stay as measured).
- Teaching: one Coach line (P18-27's table, saved in `Progress.d.tips`, shown once on the first time a player's own spark gets a second link): `chain` "Sparks and fire spread. Each link in a chain is counted." (55 characters, ASCII, device-neutral). One Training scenario (a 7th entry in `SCENARIOS` 13240, "7: A chain", loader `scenario(n)` 11257, key 7: the key regex `/^Digit[1-6]$/` at 13597, the "also keys 1-6" text at 14417 and `tscenGo` at 13715): the player stands within a strike of the level's first chain post and the dummy in its zone; it is offered only on a level whose rows have an arc or fire post with something flammable or conducting beside it, and is not listed elsewhere. One help line in the Help text (P16-04): "Chain: scenery that sets off scenery. Look for panels, barrels and cardboard."
- Not changed: Settings (no new row; Hazards, Breakables and Items rules of Free Fight, P18-43, switch it off by removing its parts: no hazards, no chain; no breakables, no burn, no collapse), `fightGrade`, the CPU, the AI, the controls, any cost, any damage number, the ring, the camera, the levels (BP-P18-13 owns the rows).
- Rejected inside C: a chain bonus in the grade (changes P14-01; the results line is enough); a chain multiplier on damage (the zone's damage is the level designer's number and both sides take it); a chain meter or a new bar (a gauge exists: Momentum); a lights-out or alarm chain (P18-12 rejected them); chain-specific CPU play (the CPU already lures to posts and leaves zones; measured first, see the balance check); a separate "chain" mode (not a mode).

- Touch, gamepad, keyboard: nothing new to press; the spark is the strike, the throw or the knock the game already has. The popup is the one used for "WALL SLAM" and "CRASH"; at 390x844 and 844x390 it sits at world height 1.0 to 2.0 above the link, never on the HUD. The Training scenario is picked in the same menu on all three inputs (key 7 on a keyboard, the row on touch and gamepad).
- Determinism, replay, online: the link fields and the `cause` variable are write-only bookkeeping; the only effect on the simulation is the momentum call, a pure function of the sim's own damage, ids from a counter and no clock, no random number, no Settings value. So the same seed and inputs give the same chains on every peer. The momentum call changes outcomes of fights that contain a chain, so the recorded hazards-on fingerprints that contain a linked hit must be re-recorded once, with the list and the reason (as P18-12 does); every fingerprint without a chain, and every 1v1 recorded without hazards, must stay equal. The online task (P12-05 determinism audit) only has to carry `link` in its checksum list if it checksums object fields; nothing else.
- Performance: no per-tick cost (links are set at the step functions that run every 10 or 60 ticks, or on a trigger), no new draw call, no new particle type; the existing caps hold (`FIRE_MAX` 4, `CHAIN_MAX` 6, `CRUSH_OBJECTS` 4, `MARK_MAX` 32), and at most `CHAIN_SHOW_MAX` popups per chain (one per depth). The BREAKPOINT.benchmark (P0-04 method) must not move.
- Edge cases:

  | Case | Result |
  |---|---|
  | Hazards off (Free Fight rule, a Settings value), or the ring drops the posts | no spark, no link, no popup, no momentum |
  | Breakables off (`Arena.solid`) | no object burns or collapses; only the arc and its conductor shock exist (depth 2): a chain never passes x2, and only a conductor shock pays |
  | Items off | a panel can still be struck by a fighter's hit if the row allows it; a metal-only panel needs a metal item or an item thrown, so it cannot start; barrels and jets still can |
  | Two fighters strike the same post in one tick | the first `hazardArm` wins (it needs state `idle`); one chain, one credit |
  | A chain lit by a timer hazard | popups in the neutral colour, stats and momentum for nobody |
  | A weak deck gives way, or a break caused by a fighter's own hit | no chain starts (`link: null`) |
  | The lighter walks into their own zone | `canHurt` excludes self: the damage counts, the momentum does not |
  | A teammate is hurt by a linked zone with Friendly fire off | `by` is null for that hit (as today); no momentum |
  | The foe is already down or KO'd | `hazardHit` returns early for a terminal state (10760); no payoff |
  | Fire put out by the hydrant or extinguisher (`douse` 10705) | the object's fire and `blaze` end; the chain simply stops; no extra text |
  | Round reset in a best-of | burning objects keep `link` and credit (10492); new objects start with `link: null` |
  | Replay, Training with infinite health, CPU vs CPU (`SimRunner`) | the stats listeners run in a headless run (they are in `MatchSim.subscribe`), the popup and sound listeners do not; the numbers are available to the balance run |
  | Versus seat 2, co-op seats | same rules; each fighter earns its own momentum and stats |
  | Reduced motion on | no camera nudge (`Camera.impact` returns early); popups stay |

- Bytes (LF, estimated; file 1,178,914 at 2041038; budget 4,000,000):

  | Part | Bytes |
  |---|---|
  | Link bookkeeping: `link`, `cause`, `nextLink` helper, 7 call sites (`hazardArm`, `hazardStart`, `stepFire` twice, `dropSupported`/`breakDeck`/collapse queue, `stepCollapse`), `link: null` in `makeObject` (3256) | 650 |
  | Conductor link (the shock reached through a conductor passed to `hazardHit`) and the burn link (`f.burnLink`, `BURN_SRC.link`) | 250 |
  | Stats (3 fields in `newStats`) and the momentum call in `hazardHit` | 260 |
  | Display: `chainLink` event, popup with the per-depth gate, sound motif, camera nudge | 510 |
  | Results line, `Progress.d.chainBest` and its cleaner | 380 |
  | Coach line | 140 |
  | Training scenario 7 (text, loader, key regex, list) and the scenario-list test site | 510 |
  | Help line | 150 |
  | **Total** | **about 2,850**; cap for the task 3,200 holds |

  Fallbacks if over the cap, in this order: drop the camera nudge (about 90); drop the Training scenario and keep the Coach line (about 450); shorten the results line (about 100). The links and the momentum rule are not dropped without asking the owner.
- Self-tests the build must add (names start `Street Chain (P18-14):`; none may skip, weaken or delete an older test):
  1. Links in order: on a level with P18-12's W1 rows, a scripted spark at the W1 panel gives ignite `cardboardC` at depth 2 and spread to `crateD` at depth 3 (plus depth 2 on each conductor the arc energises), each with the lighter's index; the same seed twice gives the same ids and depths;
  2. One case per link kind (arc, conductor shock, ignite, spread, fall, crush, burn), table driven; a fighter's plain strike on a breakable is not a link; a burnt-out object with nothing on it adds no depth;
  3. Off switches: Hazards off, ring drops the posts, Breakables off (no link beyond the arc), an idle fight with no spark (no event, no stat);
  4. Credit and pay: a linked zone hurting a foe gives the lighter `Combat.momentum` exactly as a strike of the same damage would (compare to the gauge change of a strike); depth 1 pays nothing; self, a teammate (Friendly fire off), a null `by` pay nothing; Friendly fire on pays a teammate-hit as `canHurt` says; for a crush hit `f.lastFoe` becomes the lighter (6928);
  5. Stats and save: `chains`, `chainMax`, `chainDmg` per fighter; results line only when `chainMax >= 2`; `Progress.d.chainBest` cleaned (missing, wrong type, negative, huge); an old save loads with 0;
  6. Text: popup strings, the Coach line (at most 70 characters, plain ASCII, the P17-05 design-note scan) and the help line; the Coach line shows once and not for the CPU, seat 2 or a replay (P18-48's rules);
  7. Training scenario 7: loads on a level with a chain post, places the fighters, is not listed on a level without one;
  8. Fingerprints: every recorded fingerprint without a linked hit equals the old value; the ones that change are listed in the test with the reason;
  9. CPU: across 20 seeds of KAI against KAI at Hard on each chain level, no fighter stays inside a linked zone after its warning (the P18-12 `leaveHazard` test, extended), and at least one chain of depth 2 or more starts somewhere in the 20 (report how many; the CPU does not have to start any);
  10. Layout at 390x844 and 844x390 in the browser run: the popup does not cover the stamina bar, the buttons or the hint strip; a chain of 4 links in a row stays readable;
  11. Balance run (below), recorded in the log.
- Balance check the build runs and records (method of P0-06, `BREAKPOINT.simulate`, KAI against KAI, 600 seeds per chain level, Easy, Normal, Hard, Expert): the seat band stays inside the recorded one (40 to 60 percent at Hard and Expert, 35 to 65 percent at Easy and Normal, REFERENCE line 1774); the share of all damage that came from linked zones is at most 10 percent; match length changes by at most 5 percent against the same seeds before the momentum call (switch the call off with a test hook, not a Setting); the boost (Momentum) starts per fight no more than 1 more time on average than before. If any cell fails, move the rule (for example, pay only from depth 3, or half the strike rate), not the CPU or the level rows.
- What the owner can change (each is one line or one row): the pick (A on its own is already tasked; B, D or E replace C); whether the chain pays Momentum at all (remove the call, 120 bytes less); the pay rate (the strike rate now) and the minimum depth (2 now); whether a chain counts in the grade (no now); the name CHAIN; the camera nudge; whether the Training scenario ships; whether neutral (null-credit) chains show; whether the results line shows for 1-link sparks (no now).
- Rejected as the X-factor (and why):
  - **Challenge codes with verifiable replays** ("every fight is a code": the input log of a fight packed as text, a friend plays the same setup and the game re-runs the log to check the result): needs the determinism audit (P12-05) and the lockstep work first, and 1 to 3 KB of text per fight is long for a message; it is the right extension of option D after online play exists, not before.
  - **A comeback state** (Tekken 8 Heat and Rage, a Blazin' Move): the Momentum boost and the ultimate (P18-07 to P18-09) are that; a second one would compete with them. Tell P18-08 that chain damage now pays Momentum.
  - **Style clash** (a type chart between the 16 styles): a fixed advantage table breaks the Block-versus-Sway 45 to 55 percent split and the owner's "balanced" rule, and P17-09 already makes the styles distinct.
  - **Rewind or retry from here** (the simulation is deterministic, so it could rewind): fits Training and an easy Arcade, but it is offline-only and a free retry already exists (Continue Arcade); not an identity.
  - **Injuries that carry across the Arcade run**: a balance burden on every stage and on the story rewrite (P18-35).
  - **Aging on death** (Sifu's hook): copying another game's hook is against the rule for this task, and P1-03 already rejected it as a duplicate of the Age slider.
  - **The crowd as a living ring** (Def Jam's crowd shoves, holds and arms fighters): the crowd is drawing only by decision R8 and making it a body changes the camera and the nav map.
  - **A new on-screen button for anything**: none of the above needs one.
- Open for the owner (each is decided above and can be changed): (1) the pick: C recommended, A is already tasked and ships anyway; D is the best second; (2) Momentum pay on chain damage (yes) and its minimum depth (2); (3) whether chain claims may be used in the store text ("Light the street" yes; "first game with chain reactions" no); (4) if the owner wants D later, it needs P12-05 first and a new SHARE_VERSION (7560) and CUSTOM_STORE_VERSION (7537).

#### The build task (proposed row)

- Row for `TASKS.md` (after BP-P18-15, the last row of Stage 13, before BP-P13-02): `- [ ] **BP-P18-49** Implement P18-14: Street Chain, the X-factor after BP-P18-14, BP-P18-13, BP-P18-48 [json](tasks/BP-P18-49.json)`.
- id: **BP-P18-49**. title: **Implement P18-14: Street Chain, the X-factor**. depends_on: **BP-P18-14** (the owner's pick recorded in this entry; BP-P18-14 stays open with `human_intervention.required` true until then), **BP-P18-13** (the environment rows W1, S2, G2, C1, R1, P2 and the hydrant), **BP-P18-48** (the Coach table and the `tips` field). Not blocked by P18-07, P18-09 or P18-24. One batch: Sonnet implementer (effort high), then Opus reviewer (effort high) until PASS, then the browser self-test, tick, commit by path.
- objective: Implement the Street Chain of Appendix C P18-14: carry the cause of every scenery effect on a `link` field and a `cause` variable; name, count and show the chain as CHAIN xN; pay the lighter Momentum for damage that a linked zone, conductor shock, burn or crush does to a foe; count chains in the stats, the results line and `Progress.d.chainBest`; teach it with one Coach line, one Training scenario and one help line. No new button, no Settings row, no grade change, no new random number.
- acceptance criteria:

  | ID | Criterion | Verification |
  |---|---|---|
  | AC-001 | Each link kind (arc, conductor shock, ignite, spread, fall, crush, burn) produces a link with the right depth and the lighter's index, and the chain number is the depth of its deepest link; a plain strike on a breakable and a burnt-out object with nothing on it are not links; the same seed gives the same links | self-tests 1 and 2, in the browser run |
  | AC-002 | A linked zone, conductor shock, burn or crush that hurts a foe pays the lighter Momentum exactly as a strike of that damage; depth 1, self, teammates with Friendly fire off and null credit pay nothing | self-test 4 |
  | AC-003 | Hazards off and the ring that drops the posts give no chain; Breakables off gives no link beyond depth 2 (arc and conductor shock only); every recorded fingerprint without a linked hit is unchanged, and each changed one is listed with its reason | self-tests 3 and 8; the full self-test |
  | AC-004 | The chain reads on a phone: popup text, sound motif, camera nudge off under Reduced motion, no overlap with the HUD at 390x844 and 844x390; stats, results line and `chainBest` work and an old save loads | self-tests 5 and 10; Playwright screenshots at both sizes, looked at |
  | AC-005 | One Coach line (at most 70 characters, ASCII, once), one Training scenario 7 on chain levels only, one help line | self-tests 6 and 7 |
  | AC-006 | Balance: the 600-seed KAI-against-KAI runs on every chain level and difficulty stay inside the seat band, linked damage is at most 10 percent of all damage, match length moves at most 5 percent, the CPU does not stay in a linked zone; numbers recorded in Appendix C as built | `BREAKPOINT.simulate` run (P0-06), numbers in the log; self-test 9 |
  | AC-007 | Performance and size: the P0-04 benchmark no worse than before, no new draw call; size at most base + 3,200 bytes and at most 4,000,000 | `BREAKPOINT.benchmark`; the node size one-liner |
  | AC-008 | Full browser self-test passes with 0 skipped and a test count that grew by the new tests; the P16-03 owner list gets: on a phone, light the Warehouse stock with a thrown metal item at the panel and read CHAIN x2 and x3; try Training scenario 7; turn Reduced motion on and check no camera nudge | browser self-test (Playwright, Chrome); the P16-03 task text |

- Build notes: (a) data first: `link: null` in `makeObject` 3256, `linkSeq` next to `hazardSeq` (9807), `newStats` 9857; (b) the `nextLink(cause, by)` helper and `MatchSim.cause`, set and cleared around `stepFire`, `stepCollapse` and the objects they touch, and mirrored to `Arena.cause` for `breakObject` 3407, `dropSupported` 3500 and the collapse queue push 3482 (set before the call and cleared after it on every path, including an early return); (c) spark sites via `hazardArm` 10527, and `hazardBreak` 10574 directly; the arc loop in `hazardStart` 10540; `ignite` 10684 gets the cause as an argument; (d) the `chainLink` event and its listeners next to `objBreak` at 13294 (popup), 13070 (sound) and next to 12777, calling `Camera.impact` (2574); (e) the momentum call in `hazardHit` 10759 to 10775, after `f.lastFoe = by` and before the KO test; (f) results line (14429), `Progress.fresh` 946 and its cleaner (962 to 963, the `seenClinch` pattern); (g) Coach line in P18-48's table; (h) `SCENARIOS` 13240, `scenario(n)` 11257, the key regex at 13597 and the "1-6" text at 14417 (and `tscenGo` 13715); update the scenario-list check at `breakpoint-tests.js`:1018 (`SCENARIOS.length !== 6`) to the new list (an intended change, named in the commit); (i) tests, then the balance run.

### P18-45 built: Tournament Ring-out row

- The Tournament join screen has a Ring-out row (Off, On) after Entrants and Difficulty; it is hidden when a saved bracket is continued, like the other two. A tap, the arrow keys and a gamepad change it through `changeLocal('tring')`; `Game.saveLevel` stores it with the Difficulty as `setups.tournament.ringOut` (a boolean), `Game.loadLevels` reads it into `selection.tournamentRing`.
- The bracket carries it: `Tournament.draw` (`options.ringOut`, only `true` counts), `blank`, `pack` and `clean` (`t.ringOut`). A saved bracket without a boolean `ringOut` takes the saved Tournament row when it is cleaned (so an old bracket gets the old Settings value, seeded below), and the next save pins it. `Tournament.simulate` and `beginTournamentMatch` read `t.ringOut` (`ring` and `ringOut` the same), so a continued bracket, the CPU fights and the live bouts agree.
- Settings: `SETTING_DEFS.ringOut` and its row are gone. `Setups.init` seeds `setups.tournament.ringOut` once, when it is not a boolean, from the old `ringOut` switch in `breakpoint.v1.settings` (read raw before any `Settings.save` can drop it), next to the Free Fight rules seed, and changes nothing else; an entry with an unknown `v` is left alone. `Game.beginMatch` no longer reads a setting: a start without `ringOut` is the whole room (Free Fight and the Tournament pass their own).
- Text: the mode description and the join screen hint name the row, not the Settings.
- Tests: three named `Tournament ring-out (P18-45):` (the bracket stores, saves and cleans it and an old or damaged one takes the saved row, Settings has no row; the join screen row on a gamepad, arrow keys and taps, saved with the Difficulty, hidden with a saved bracket, carried by the draw and its save; the start-up seed). Updated, not weakened: "Arena bounds (P17-08)" plain 1v1 (now whole room whatever an old value holds) and Tournament bout (the bracket decides, an opposite old value is ignored), the ring test that checked `SETTING_DEFS.ringOut` (now checks it is gone), the P11-02 title, the seeded walk and the hash test no longer set the removed key.
- Size: +710 LF bytes in `breakpoint.html` (1,178,914 to 1,179,624).

### P18-21 built: Arcade goons, allies and Survival brawls (P18-20 + P18-37)

- Goons (`goonRecord`, `goonProfile`, `GOON_VARIANTS`, `GOON_SCALE`, `breakpoint.html` before `const Story`): a crew is built in code in the creator's record format from any `ROSTER` id (colours, move style and defense of the theme; a missing or bare-top colour is the neutral grey `#808894`); 3 variants (BRUISER, SCRAPPER, RUNNER) and a leader, ids `g:0`, `g:1`, `g:2`, `g:L`, no custom slot, no `ROSTER` entry, no `rank`. Every record passes `validateCustom` (tested for all 32 themes). Points 35 / 34 / 35 / 38 (budget 36, leader 38), every attribute 3 to 7, speed at least 4.
- Sim: `cfg.goons` (theme id) and `cfg.goonLeader` (name). `waveProfiles` deals the variants by the running `waveCursor % 3` (no random number, same crew every try) and puts the leader goon in slot 0 of the leader row (`cfg.rival` still wins when set). `MatchSim.crewScale` applies the table at the CPU level (health x0.30 / 0.32 / 0.275 / 0.16 for Easy / Normal / Hard / Expert, damage x0.50 / 0.48 / 0.455 / 0.32 before the level's `dmg`, stamina x0.8; re-fitted in the review, see "Review fit" below; the leader 2x health and 1.3x damage) in the constructor and in `enterEnemy`. Non-Arcade brawls keep the roster cycle.
- Story: stage 1 rival A's crew (leader row cut as before), stage 3 the boss's crew with its leader goon (`waveBeat` still fires on it), stage 5 the champion's, stage 6 the champion's after "Offer a hand" (also with no choice) with rival A as an ally, rival A's own crew led by rival A himself (an unscaled roster profile) after "Walk away". `waveCut` is no longer set by the story (the engine keeps it). Rival B is gone from `Story.start`, `pack` and `restore`; an old save's `rivalB` is ignored. The leader's name is `Story.leaderName(run, crew)` (`NAME_IDEAS` without GRANITE, index `(seed + 5 x crew) % 28`); B7's `R2` is the leader goon (`Story.profileOf`, `idOf('R2')` is `g:L`, token `{rival2}` kept). Stage info reads "led by <leader>" for stages 3, 5 and 6 and "with <rival A>" on stage 6 after the hand.
- Allies (`cfg.allies`, up to 2 roster ids, never the player): `MatchSim.allies`, `peopleCount` (people first, then allies; `partySize` counts both, one more enemy per ally in every wave, as decided), an `AIController` at the run's level, the level's `dmg` factor, no stamina edge (`giveStaminaEdge` loop over people only), full health at every start (`placeFighters`), `playersAlive()` for the loss rule (only a person counts when there are allies; the clock still beats the people). HUD: the ally's tag reads ALLY and carries a health bar.
- Survival: `Survival type` row after Difficulty (Duels, Brawls, Brawls + 1 ally, Brawls + 2 allies; tap, left and right; saved as `setups.survival.type`, 0 to 3, anything else 0). Duels are the old code path (`survivalCpu` is the old rung line moved into a method; same draw order and fingerprints). Brawls (`nextSurvivalBrawl`): enemies by CPU level and allies exactly as the decided table (min of 6), drawn in turn from the lap with no fighter twice in a fight even across a lap end, allies after the enemies; `cfg.mode: 'brawl'` with `cfg.survival`; group health `SURVIVAL_GROUP` (x0.50, 0.40, 0.33, 0.28, 0.24 for 2 to 6 enemies, 1 for 1), damage x0.7 (`crewScale`); clock `max(30, 50 - 2 x extra) + 8 x (enemies - 1)`; heal `0.25 + 0.04 x (enemies - 1) - 0.02 x extra`. Records: `Progress.d.survivalRec` (three `[wins, seconds]` pairs, clamped field by field in `Progress.init`), Duels keep `survivalKills` and `survivalSeconds`; `Progress.counter(name)` is the one reader for the unlock counters (`streak` = larger of Duels and Brawls without an ally); an ally fight saves no grade; results say "Fights won" and the HUD "FIGHT n" for the brawl types; the mode list shows the best of the selected type.
- Tests (5, names start `Arcade goons (P18-21):` x3, `Allies (P18-21):`, `Survival brawls (P18-21):`): all crews against `validateCustom`, budget, theme and ids; the factor table at every level, goons below every main fighter, the leader above its crew, variants dealt in turn, same cfg (also through JSON) same crew; the map of crews to bosses for every preset and 3 clears, the cap of 3 main fighters, the leader rows, Walk away, an old save with `rivalB`; allies (stage 6 with and without the choice, party, health, stamina, who may hurt whom, person down, at most 2, a headless stage 6); Survival (enemy table for all levels and types, no repeats also at a lap end, group factors, ally strength and carried health, the saved type with hostile values, records per type, damaged `survivalRec`, the streak counter). Updated to the new flow, not weakened: the unlock test (stage 3 now opens DMITRI and LARS; no rival B), the story rivals test (no `rivalB`), the choice test (the hand gives an ally instead of `waveCut`), the cast and allowed-`cfg`-keys tests, the stage 6 wave rows and the stage 3 leader.

An ally lowers the clear rate of the AI person at Hard and Expert; Normal is in step. The likely cause is the AI person and the AI ally competing for the same attack tokens (`CrowdDirector`), which a human does not do, but this was not tried out. ### P18-53 built: hit freeze with more than two fighters

- Owner 2026-11-07: in a Free Fight free-for-all of 4 CPUs and the owner, a CPU's strong hit froze the whole fight ("this abrupt timestop ... disoriented me"); the owner asked for the best rule for modes with more people and delegated the pick ("go with the best choice").
- Decision: a 1v1 keeps every freeze as before. With more than two fighters a freeze stops everyone, so only a hit the one person lands or takes freezes, at most `CROWD_HITSTOP_MAX` (4) ticks; with two or more people, and on every CPU against CPU hit, nothing freezes (flash, shake, sound and rumble still mark the hit). It depends only on the seats, so replays stay the same.
- Code: `MatchSim.addHitStop(ticks, att, def)` replaces the 15 direct `match.hitStop` writes; test `Hit freeze (P18-53)`. Chrome self-test 625 of 625 with no fingerprint change (the fingerprint fights are 1v1s).

### P18-01 built: movement speed +10 percent

- Owner 2026-11-01 and 2026-11-04: fighters "a little faster", "movement is too slow". Decision: every walk and run speed +10 percent (the start value P18-01 named); +20 percent was tried first and dropped (11 tests broke: CPU spacing, deck legs, item throws, hazard shares).

| What | Before | After | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `WALK_FORWARD` | 2.2 m/s | 2.4 | owner: movement too slow |
| `WALK_BACK` | 1.6 | 1.75 | same share, backing off stays slower than closing in |
| `WALK_SIDE` | 1.8 | 2.0 | same share |
| `RUN_SPEED` | 4.6 | 5.0 | same share; sidestep (7.0) unchanged |
| `AI_TOSS_OPEN_TICKS` (new) | none | Easy 1800 (30 s), others 0 | Easy opens with fists: at the faster walk the shorter Easy fights threw 0.44 per team-minute over the P18-34 seeded set, above the 0.35 cap (old code 0.24, 3 throws in 12.4 team-minutes; faster walk alone 5 in 11.4; with the wait 4 in 13.2 = 0.30). The Easy takes came only 5 to 7 ticks sooner, so the cause is fight length and one more throw, not item reach; one throw moves the rate about 0.08 |

- Ranges and AI spacing: the spacing bands work on distance; the edge and ring look-aheads are checked every tick (a run moves 0.083 m a tick, the 0.9 m run look keeps about 11 ticks of margin). Nothing else scales with walk speed.

### P18-16 start side (decided and built 2026-11-09)

- Decision (the recommended one of BR-001, nothing changed): the start side is offered in Free Fight, Arcade duels and Training. "Automatic" stays the default, so the P9 seat balance and every recorded fingerprint hold when nobody picks a side.
  - Free Fight has had the row since P18-43 ("Player 1 starts", the last row of More options). This task adds the same row, with the same name and labels, to Arcade (the fighter screen, under Difficulty) and to Training (the setup screen, above the sparring partners). It is an ordinary spinbutton row, so a tap, the arrow keys and a gamepad all step it; no new button.
  - Automatic: today's rule exactly (a 1v1 draws the first fighter's side from the match seed in round 1 and swaps it every round; `cfg.sides`, `MatchSim.sideFor`; no random number). Training never drew a side (it always started left), so its Automatic is Left and its row offers Left and Right only, default Left.
  - Left or Right: the first fighter (player 1) starts there in round 1 and the sides swap every round after, as now. Training has no rounds, so its choice holds.
  - Two people: the row is player 1's side, so two people can never pick the same one; player 2 takes the other side. The CPU takes the other side. Arcade has one person.
  - Arcade: the choice is part of the story run (`Story.start` takes it, `Story.pack` and `Story.clean` keep it, so Continue Arcade plays on with it). It sets round 1 of the duel stages 2, 4 and 7 (`Story.cfg` gives them `startSide`; `Story.cast` stands the scene's cast there); the brawl stages still start on the left. A save from before the row reads as Automatic.
  - Not offered: Versus, Survival and Tournament (every bout keeps the drawn side, which is what keeps their seats fair), and lineups of three or more teams and the crowd (Free Fight dims the row, P18-43).
- Config and saving: `cfg.startSide` (0 drawn, 1 left, -1 right) is the field Free Fight already used; `MatchSim.startSide()` now also reads it in Training. The Arcade and Training choices are saved as `setups.arcade.side` and `setups.training.side` (0 Automatic, 1 Left, 2 Right) beside Difficulty, only when they are not the default, and read back by `Game.loadLevels`; a missing or damaged value reads as the default.
- Balance: nothing moves when nobody picks a side (Automatic runs the code it ran before; the pinned fingerprints and the seat-balance tests pass unchanged). A chosen side is a choice of the level's lopsidedness for round 1 only, so it carries the seat effect of that level for one round of a best-of-3 (the swap gives the other side in round 2). Measured with the headless runner (`SimRunner.run`, KAI against KAI, Hard, items and hazards on, no ring, seeds 1 to 60 per cell, default rounds, so the side holds in round 1 only; the heavy slots were busy, so the sample is 60 and one standard error is about 6 points; first fighter wins, left / right / Automatic): Warehouse 33 / 55 / 43 %, Dojo 38 / 58 / 40, Pit 48 / 58 / 55, Rooftop 57 / 35 / 43, Subway 42 / 67 / 57, Garage 70 / 38 / 55, Construction 40 / 45 / 38, Club 55 / 50 / 55; pooled over the eight levels (480 matches per column) 47.9 / 50.8 / 48.3 %. So a chosen side tilts single levels by up to about 20 points from even (Garage 70 % on the left, Subway 67 % on the right), the two sides cancel over the levels, and Automatic stays inside the same band; no level or number was changed, because the choice is the player's and one round of a best-of-3.
- Tests (3, 'Start side (P18-16)'): the sim (Free Fight, Arcade and Training, two levels, four seeds: Left, Right, drawn and unset in rounds 1 to 3; Training holds); the story run (duel stages have the side and the cast stands on it, brawl stages and an Automatic run have none, pack and restore keep it, damaged values read as Automatic, the stage fight opens and swaps); the rows (a tap, the arrow keys and a gamepad on Arcade and on Training, the labels, the saved value read back, damaged values, the Arcade run and the Training fight take the side).
- File size: stored LF `breakpoint.html` 1,209,623 -> 1,211,803 bytes (+2,180); the budget is 4,000,000.
- Owner device check for P16-03: on a phone, step the Start side row on the Arcade fighter screen and the Training setup screen by tap; start a duel and a Training fight on each side.

### P18-54 (with P18-51 and P18-35) Arcade story rebuilt from fighting-game tropes (2026-11-09)

- Owner (verbatim): 2026-11-09 "source the narrative,story from games that provide influence (tekken,urban reign etc) / We will rework the story using tropes from scratch. Currently its 100% ai sounding"; 2026-11-07 "Rewrite the story/Arcade to be human sounding. It still sounds ai made"; 2026-11-03 "The dialog in story beats is cheesy and definitely reads as AI made it and without cohesion". Research: Appendix B, "P18-54 - Story tropes of the reference games". Nothing supernatural is used.
- Tropes picked, and why they fit the data the game already has:

  | Trope (Appendix B) | Where it sits in a run | Why |
  |---|---|---|
  | A belt whose owner has his own reasons; family money behind it | ZERO's city belt; ZERO's family owns the club building and its roof (stages 5 to 7) | the run already ends with ZERO on the rooftop after a club night; ZERO's origin is Wealthy family, his goal Stay undefeated |
  | Underground fight clubs owned by bosses, climbed place by place | gym (stage 2), the Pit (stage 4), the club (stage 6), the roof (stage 7) | the four fixed levels of the run are already that ladder |
  | One crew per boss, the crew goes first | rival A's crew at home (1), the Pit boss's crew (3), ZERO's crew (5, 6) | P18-20 + P18-37: every boss brings their own goons |
  | The rival who becomes an ally or turns on you | B5 choice, B12 and stage 6 | "Offer a hand" puts rival A beside you, "Walk away" brings rival A's crew against you (P18-21) |
  | The final fight at the top of the boss's building | stage 7 on ZERO's roof | the rooftop level |
  | The boss who taught the champion | HAO taught ZERO (and every belt holder) to fall at the Pit | HAO is 57, Wing Chun, Martial arts family |
  | Debt, missing sibling, revenge with names, police family, the old champion's last run | the 24 goals and origins | the goal and origin lists already hold these; the lines make them concrete |
  | Fighters from many countries, each with a private reason | Country, Origin and Goal | the three choices of the creator |

- Story bible:
  - The city is the player's own ({city}: the country's city). Fight money there runs through one belt. ZERO (33, karate, masked, Wealthy family, never lost) holds it; his family owns the building with the Night Club and the roof. ZERO only fights people the Pit sends up, and only on his roof.
  - Below the club is the Pit, a boiler-room cage. Three old hands each run one night of it and take the door money: HAO has Thursdays, MARLON Fridays, YOAV Saturdays. Whose night you get is the run's boss (the region and the clears pick it, as before). Above the Pit is legal sport: the City Fight Gym, where rival A trains and where the belt queue starts.
  - Why the fights happen: the belt pays, and the only road to it is gym, then Pit, then club, then roof. Every name on that road has a crew that fights for them in the street, so a new name meets a crew before each door.
  - The three bosses and what each wants: HAO (57, Wing Chun) taught ZERO to fall on the Pit floor before the family bought better coaches; he wants to see someone take ZERO apart, but only someone who can get past him. His B9 line says everyone who has worn the belt learned to fall on his floor, so it also holds in ZERO's own run. MARLON (49, Kali, dockhand) runs Fridays like a dock shift and hands half his door to the club every week; he wants someone worth sending up who will cost the club. YOAV (34, Krav Maga, reservist) works security for ZERO's family; the Pit is a paid shift and stopping people going up is his job; he wants to do it well and go home.
  - The champion: ZERO in every run except ZERO's own, where MARA holds the belt (P10-02). Lines that name the champion use the new `{champ}` token, so they stay true for MARA; only goals no ZERO run can have (Win the title, Beat the champion, Earn respect) name ZERO. One character is the same in every run: DEACON works nights in his own run too, DIEGO has four hundred followers as a player and four hundred watching as a rival.
  - Rival A (by the goal's motive) mirrors the player's reason: DEACON (title: twenty years of bakery night shifts for one more go at the belt), FEMKE (body: counts every wasted step), DIEGO (fame: streams everything, even from his sock), KELSEY (past: did three years in the Pit, worked the club door, got out), GIORGI (family: eleven cousins, takes a walk-off as an insult), ROXY (bond: came because she was bored and loves the bit where it goes wrong). Rival A now always says their own lines, also when they stand in for a player whose motive names that player (DEACON, DIEGO and KELSEY's own runs).
  - The leader goon (B7, `{rival2}`) is the Pit boss's man and talks about his boss; crews never speak.
  - Origin sets the tone (rough, ordinary, strict) and with it who is around the fighter: rough has no safety net (sofas, changed locks, clips filmed by strangers), ordinary has family (an aunt who rings, frozen peas, a mum who asks), strict has rules (letters, an old coach's texts, drills). The B1 line says where the fighter comes from in one fact.
  - Goal sets the reason and the through-line: B2 states it with one concrete thing (a cleared space on a wall, a date in pen on a hand, three emails), B10 (after the Pit) moves it on with the same thing, B14 (on the roof) answers it with the same thing again.
  - One line per preset: KAI mops the gym he trains in and takes everything literally. MARA keeps her kid's drawings in her kit bag and says out loud it's for the rent. BRUTUS is big and quiet, owes a loan shark and says sorry after he hits you. YUKI is small and fast and keeps a list of everyone who said no. DMITRI works at a steel plant and rings his mother after every fight. ZERO has never lost, partly because his family never let him meet anyone who could beat him. DEACON bakes on nights and lost a belt final long ago. ROSA runs the family grill and someone is leaning on it. HAO keeps the Thursday Pit and once taught ZERO. FEMKE counts reps, steps and seconds and has no small talk. PRANEE was turned away by every gym and doesn't smile in photos. LARS does payroll, joined on doctor's orders and is surprised he's good. AMARA grew up in a police house and knows the crews' names from the files. SORA talks too much and wants people at her birthday. DIEGO delivers food and streams every fight from his handlebars. TIAGO runs a free kids' class and counts the coins in the jar. KELSEY got out of the Pit and came back to set something right. ELISE has a new name and always sits facing the door. NARAN came from the steppe with one bag and says very little. GIORGI wears the ushanka, has eleven cousins and wants the man who hurt his brother. ARMINE shows her brother's photo to everyone at the Pit. REID's coach died owing the belt a rematch. CAMILA has TV parents and came to get fit, then stayed for the chokes. VIKRAM works a wedding-hall door and knows when not to fight. LUCIA makes pastry and her nonna thinks she does yoga. MARLON keeps the Friday Pit and wants his half back. NIA is nineteen and looking for her sister. YOAV works the Saturday shift for ZERO's family. KASIA does two jobs at a bottling plant and fights on her day off. CRUZ has ZERO's poster in his locker with the eyes scratched out. TESSA drove twelve hours from the farm for the belt. ROXY laughs when she gets hit.
- Method (P18-35: one voice, one through-line): every beat follows from the one before it. Stage 1 is rival A's crew at home, so B3 names rival A and the City Fight Gym; B4 and B5 are rival A; B6 is rival A pointing at the Pit and the boss's crew; B7 is that crew's leader talking about the boss; B8 is the cost of stage 3 the night before the Pit; B9 is the boss's night at the Pit; B10 is the goal after the Pit; B11 is the champion's crew at your door; B12 is rival A again (beside you or against you); B13 is the champion on the roof; B14 answers B2 with the same object; B16 answers B1: each region now has an epilogue line set in the same place as its opening (the car park, the underpass tape, the cafe). The setbacks return: B8 before the Pit, B15 after any lost stage, B16's continues line.
- Voice rules used on every line (P18-51): plain British English as the game already used, short sentences, contractions, one concrete thing a line (a bakery, a sock, a bedsheet, a receipt), people answer their own worry instead of the question (KELSEY, GIORGI, DIEGO), threats said as jobs or bets (YOAV, the leader goon), no speech about what fighting means, no tidy moral, no rule-of-three lists, none of journey, destiny, legacy, rise, forge, embrace, unleash, testament, no em-dash rhythm, not every line a joke (B1, B8 and most B14 lines are plain, and boxes do not all end on a short punchline). Each line was checked for a detail only Breakpoint has (its levels, its fighters, the Pit nights). A script checked every line at its limit with the longest tokens (90 characters, origins 64, creator hints 60) and for non-ASCII characters before the game file was written.
- Data and code (no key, condition or speaker removed; no beat added):
  - `STORY_REGION_LIST` gains a column `end` (the B16 box, ref `$home`); B16.1 keeps its three tone rows (and their poses) and now shows the region's epilogue.
  - `STORY_MOTIVES` gains `hand` and `walk` (rival A's B12 lines, refs `$hand` and `$walk`); B12.1 keeps its two choice rows.
  - `Story.beat` takes `$challenge`, `$beaten`, `$hand`, `$walk` and `$p4` from the motive row whose rival is the run's rival A (fallback: the run's motive), so a stand-in rival says their own lines.
  - New token `{champ}` (the champion's name, ZERO or MARA) in `Story.tokens`.
  - `Story.stageInfo` names whose crew a brawl is: "DEACON's crew, the first three waves", "HAO's crew, all the waves led by TANK", "ZERO's crew, all the waves led by ..., with DEACON" (hand) and "DEACON's crew, all the waves led by DEACON" (walk).
  - Every origin line, goal hint, goal arc (72), rival line (24), region line and epilogue (20) and tone, boss and extra row is new. STORY_INTROS are emote labels (Nod, Glove tap, ...) and stay.
  - Tests: "Story (P10-03): the data" also checks the region epilogues and the B12 lines at their limits and knows `{champ}`; new "Story (P18-54)" checks rival A's own lines for all 32 presets with both choices, DEACON's stand-in (FEMKE), B1 and B16 in the same place, no token or ref left unfilled in any box, `{champ}` (MARA in ZERO's run) and the stage lines; "Story settings (P6-10)" looks for the new flawless line ("Not one round. Hang on.") instead of the old text.

### P18-40 critical issue sweep (2026-11-05)

- Result: 1 Critical and 1 High found and fixed (the first review of this sweep found them; the first pass of the sweep had listed both as "seen, not critical"). Critical = a mode or choice that cannot be used, a soft lock (no way forward or back), lost progress, a crash. The sweep covered the main menu, the mode list and the eight modes (Arcade, Survival, Training, Free Fight, Versus, Brawl, Co-op Brawl, Tournament with Continue tournament), their fighter, rules, Players and teams, arena, join and bracket screens, fights (win, loss, clock, Quit from pause), results, Rematch, Change fighters, Continue and Main menu, and Controls, Move list, Settings, Unlocks, About and the creator (with its Fight preview) on keyboard 1, keyboard 2, gamepad and touch / mouse.

| ID | Sev | Area | Location | Reproduction | Cause and fix | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| E01 | Critical | Lost progress | `UI.confirmFighter` (Arcade), `UI.confirmTournamentPick` | Play, Enter (Arcade is the default button), Confirm with a saved Arcade run at stage 5: the run is replaced at once. The same with the last fighter confirm of a new Tournament over a saved bracket. No warning, no undo. | `startArcade` and `playTournament` write the new save as soon as they start. Fix: with a save present the confirm opens a new screen `replace` ("Replace your saved run: NAME, stage 5 of 7?" / "Replace your saved tournament: 8 fighters, next: Semi-final?") made of the game's ordinary panel and menu buttons: Keep (the default, it is Back, so Esc, B and a tap on Back all keep) returns to the fighter screen with the save and the pick as they were, Replace starts the new run. The screen has the double tap guard of Pause and Results. | [x] fixed, self-tests added |
| E02 | High | Gamepad | `UI.update` (join screen branch), `Inputs.lobbyPad`, `UI.onLobby` | Gamepad only on the Tournament or Co-op join screen: the Entrants row and the CPU level button cannot be reached or changed (the pad reads only the lobby there). | Fix: `Inputs.lobbyPad` also reports up / down (focus moves) from any gamepad, joined or not, left / right from a gamepad that has not joined (`adjust`; a joined one's `cycle` is the same press) and A on a joined one (`press`). `UI.onLobby`: up / down move the focus; left / right from a gamepad (events marked `pad`) change the Entrants row in focus (and the CPU level in a Tournament), else choose a joined pad's fighter as before; a key reaches the page twice (the lobby and `UI.onKey`, which already steps the row), so key events never change the row here (a review found Entrants stepping twice and staying put after a keyboard joined; a self-test now checks one step per press for both keyboards); A changes the row in focus once the focus was moved to it. Co-op keeps left / right for the joined pad's fighter, join, leave and Start are as before, and Tournament seat cards still do not cycle (P18-41). The hint text says so. | [x] fixed, self-test added |

- Method: 21 self-tests in the new section "Mode flows (P18-40)" of `breakpoint-tests.js`. They press only what the screen on show offers (the `data-act` of its enabled buttons: what a tap, Enter and a pad's A all press), through `UI.act`, `UI.onClick`, `UI.onKey` (Esc, arrows, Enter) and the lobby events of fake gamepads. The page is stood in for: the real `Game.go` with `GS_TRANSITIONS`, then `UI.onGameState` on stand-in elements; the screen's focusable elements are listed as `UI.navItems` lists them and `document.activeElement` follows the focus, so arrow keys and a pad's stick move it and Enter or A clicks it. A reach check fails when the keys or the pad (a pad's stick down, once per element) never land on an enabled element of a screen. Fights are played to their end by the match itself (a real knock-out or the clock, then the game loop's VICTORY to RESULTS step, Punch skipping the pose); every screen drawn is checked for a way out and for no enabled button without `data-nav`. At the end of a test on a page the game state goes to the menu the real way, so the music and the touch buttons follow the menu, and the frame loop numbers (`Game.last`, `acc`, `frameAvg`, the `Diag` frame stats) and `Game.tournamentResume` are put back.
- Tests: one flow per mode (Arcade, Arcade with all scenes to the clear and the ending, Survival, Training, Free Fight with and without a lineup, Versus, Brawl, Co-op Brawl with a keyboard and a pad, Tournament on touch to the title, Tournament left and continued, Tournament for two devices, two people in one bout); the two replace questions (Keep, Back, Esc, the pad's B, a tap straight after the question, Replace, for an Arcade run and for a bracket of one and of two); the join screens by the arrow keys and a pad (joined or not); lineups that cannot start; three and four people on pads; Back and Esc from every screen of every mode; the side screens and the creator; and seeded random walks (presses, taps and keys on option rows, Esc, joins, pauses, fights; custom fighter, saved run and bracket, story, ring-out, items and hazards settings on some seeds). After every press a walk checks: the game state and the screen agree, no state change was refused, `Diag.errors` is unchanged, a joined person is read from a device in play, the join screen has co-op input and the lobby on, and the saved progress (records, unlocks) equals the memory copy and never falls. Now and then and at the end, Back / Quit / Main menu alone must lead to the main menu.
- On the old game (HEAD) the Arcade and Tournament replace tests and the join screen test fail ("Confirm did not ask", "the confirm did not ask", "right on a gamepad that has not joined did not change Entrants"), and so does the Co-op test through its reach check ("the gamepad never reaches back"); all four pass now. Four deliberate breaks of the game made earlier (Back from the arena, the Tournament confirm, Back from the bracket, Quit in the pause menu) were each caught by 3 to 11 tests.
- Evidence: 592 walks of 100 steps passed before the fixes (seeds 1-150, 1000-1011, 2000-2199, 3000-3039, 4000-4039, 5000-5149); after them 60 more (seeds 6000-6059) with the new checks and 30 (seeds 7000-7029) with the final form of the join-screen code. The suite keeps 5 walks (seeds 1-5) because a walk costs 2 to 3 s.
- Two false alarms of the harness were found and fixed in the tests, not in the game: a walk that pressed Skip on a scene with a question never answered it (Skip still asks the answer, and the answer buttons are on screen), and a wave scene that pauses a fight (Arcade stage 3) must be played through before the match goes on.
- Seen, not critical (not fixed):
  - Co-op Brawl cannot be started with touch or mouse alone: a device has to join with Punch or A first, and "Choose arena" stays off until one has. By design (the mode list says "keyboards and gamepads", the join screen says "Touch controls are not used in co-op"); Brawl with one player covers a solo crowd fight on touch. Versus and a lineup with two or more people likewise need a second keyboard layout or a gamepad.
  - A saved Tournament bracket with two or more people waits on the join screen until as many devices have joined; with fewer devices Back is the only way on, and the bracket stays on the mode list until a new Tournament is drawn over it (which now asks first).
  - Back from a fighter screen to the mode list leaves the last `Game.run` set (Quit to main menu clears it); every mode starts its own run, so nothing reads the old one.
  - A Versus lineup that cannot start (the second slot set to CPU on Players and teams) is not stopped on the Versus rules screen: "Choose arena" is on, the arena screen's "Start fight" says why (toast) and stays, and Back leads to the lineup to fix it.
- Checks: headless run with `BP_FILTER="Mode flows"`: 21 / 21; full headless run through `heavy.mjs`: 501 / 518, exactly the 17 known failures (16 "needs the main menu", 1 "blank faces"), listeners 25 / 25 before and after; `breakpoint.html` is 1,173,238 bytes (LF, BOM counted) of 1,200,000. Still open: the same tests in Chrome (the stand-in page elements are used there too; on a page each test ends by taking the game state to the menu the real way), and the owner's device checks, which now include the replace question and a gamepad on the Tournament join screen.

### P18-38 ground submissions (2026-11-05)

- Owner, 2026-11-03: "On a ground armbar i float above the ground." Measured with the new self-test (lowest drawn part of each fighter above the floor, from the drawn matrices): armbar holder (Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu, MMA) up to +53 cm in the air, the kneeling pin (Wrestling, Judo) down to -14 cm and the Hapkido wrist lock down to -12 cm into the floor, the Sambo leg lock +1 cm, the held fighter +2 to +5 cm face up; a knocked-down or knocked-out fighter (unheld) lies 2 to 5 cm above the floor face up and 7 to 16 cm into it face down.
- Cause: `rootHeight()` puts the root where the legs of a STANDING body reach the floor, and only the `lie` blend (the knockdown pose) overrides it. The four `HOLD_POSES` (pin, leg, arm, wrist) kneel, sit or lie but set no `lie`, so the body hung at the standing height of its leg angles: the armbar lay back with its legs up and the root stayed 50 cm high. `LIE_HEIGHT` (0.17) is one value for every build, and a face-down body is deeper than a face-up one, so no single value fits.
- Fix 1 (`Fighter.animate`, `plantFloor`, `lowestPart`, `skeleton`, `part`, `probeLow`): on every tick a fighter in a hold (the holder in SUBMIT) or lying down (DOWN held or not, KO, and the GETUP out of them) is walked once without drawing (`part`, `pieces` and the held item record the lowest height of every box, ball and cylinder instead of queuing it, `PROBE_LOW`), and `plantShift` lifts or lowers the drawing so the lowest drawn part is on the floor whatever the pose, body and build. The lowest part moves to the floor from where the last tick drew it, and back to the pose's own lowest `PLANT_RELEASE_TICKS` (20) ticks after the pose ends, at most `PLANT_SPEED` (1.5 m/s, 2.5 cm a tick), so it neither sinks nor jumps while the pose blends (review finding: an ease of the shift at a fixed rate let the half-blended pose sink 16 to 18 cm into the floor and jump 13 cm in one tick at the start and the end of a hold; the first version of this fix). Everybody else is not measured, so nothing else pays for the extra pass. `frameScale` returns a reused array (the measuring pass calls it too). Drawing only: the simulation, hit boxes, timing and key points used by hits are unchanged (the key points feed only effects and scene placement).
- Fix 2 (`HOLD_POSES`): the armbar lies flat on the back (`bodyPitch` -1.5, `lie` 1, head up) with legs and arms keeping their old directions in the room (hips 1.5 and 1.3 became 0.9 and 0.7, shoulders 1.2 became 0.6, because the body lies 0.6 further back); the leg lock sits back on the floor with the legs raised (`bodyPitch` -1.1, `lie` 1); the pin kneels (knees 2.5, so the shins lie along the floor instead of a deep crouch). The wrist lock stays a low crouch, now with its feet on the floor.
- Check: `Ground submissions (P18-38)` in `breakpoint-tests.js`. Test 1 plays every style that can hold (6 styles, 4 hold poses) on the 8 test bodies, the foe face up and face down alternately, and the 3 one-handed items (bat, chain, bottle) in the holder's hand: both fighters stand 30 ticks, the foe is knocked down, Grapple 2 ticks later, 100 ticks of hold, then the holder lets go and both get up; the lowest drawn part of both is read on EVERY tick until both have stood 30 ticks. It fails if the part is deeper than 0.2 cm under the floor while lying (or under the standing stance it came from), more than 3 cm under the stance while standing, more than 3 cm above the floor 25 ticks into a lying pose, or moves more than 3 cm in one tick (the get-up is checked too). Worst after the fix: 0.0 cm in every hold and lying pose; at the start and the end of a hold the part is only at the standing stance's own toe sink (-3.4 to -8.0 cm, as when standing), and the biggest one-tick move is 2.5 cm. Test 2 checks that nobody is measured while standing and that the measuring is gone once both stand again. Test 3 lays a knocked-down and a knocked-out fighter, face up and face down, on the 8 bodies, 40 ticks after the fall (a knock-out needs 26), and needs -0.2 cm to +3 cm; on the old code it fails with +1.8 to +4.8 cm face up and -7.5 to -15.9 cm face down, after the fix every one is 0.0 cm.
- Left alone: a standing guard stance draws the toes up to 8 cm below the floor line (the standing toes were not part of this task); `LIE_HEIGHT` and `liePose` are unchanged, the shift corrects the drawn height on top of them. The flight of a throw is not corrected. The get-up now stays on the floor too (it sank 28 cm into it on the old code); for the 20 ticks the pose blends back to the stance the lowest part is held at the depth of the fighter's guard stance (`stanceLow`), not at 0, so a fighter who is up again is not lifted by his toe sink (review finding). The test also fails if a standing row is more than 3 cm above the stance, and once 25 ticks into a lying pose it needs -0.2 cm.

### P18-36 crowd camera and body stacking (2026-11-05)

- Found during P18-34: the `Brawl camera` hidden-player test (warehouse, 141 ticks in a row, limit 54) failed on seeds 3 and 8 on the code before P18-34 and on 5 and 7 after it, and the `1v6 brawl` test (two bodies closer than 0.3 m) failed on seed 2 before and on 5 and 9 after. Both tests were pinned to seed 6 to pass. They now loop over seeds 1 to 12 (`CROWD_SEEDS`); on the code before this task they fail on seeds 5 and 9 (1v6, 0.24 m and 0.22 m) and on seeds 7 and 8 (camera, warehouse, 141 and 139 ticks).
- Camera cause: the warehouse metal rack at x -10.9, z -4.0 (1.2 m x 2.6 m, 2.4 m tall) stands against the west wall. A player in the corner just behind its end (x -11.1, z -5.7) is in line with it as seen from the usual eye position (the eye is held 0.6 m off the side wall, 0.5 rad of pitch). Every pose in `CAMERA_OCCLUSION_TRIES` stayed hidden: the azimuth swing is limited to +-0.55 rad round the base (a clear view needs 1.0 to 1.4 rad from the side), and the pitch was capped at 1.15 rad (66 degrees), which still looks along the rack. The camera then waited for the enemies to move, up to 141 ticks.
- Camera fix (`CAMERA_STEEP_SWING`, `CAMERA_ELEV_STEEP_MAX`, `swungElev`, `CAMERA_OCCLUSION_TRIES`): the list ends with two nearly straight-down views, `[0, 0.9, 0]` and `[0, 0.9, 1]` (normal aim, then aimed at the players). A pitch swing of 0.9 or more may reach 1.4 rad (80 degrees); every other swing and the normal camera keep the cap `CAMERA_ELEV_MAX` of 1.15 rad (66 degrees), so every earlier pose is exactly as before (a first version of this fix raised the one cap to 1.4, which also let the 0.7 swings reach 1.16 to 1.25 rad; the review caught that). The two are tried last, so every case that was clear before behaves as before; the swing releases 0.6 s after the normal view is clear, as always. A pure pitch swing keeps the camera azimuth, so the stick directions the player has learned do not turn. The limit in the test (grace 0.3 s plus 0.6 s) is unchanged. The 1v1, Versus and Training camera does not use the swing.
- Body cause: `MatchSim.separate` skipped every pair with a THROWN body, however low it was. A body that is thrown (or juggled) lands in `afterCollision`, after the separation of that tick, so one that came down on a standing or walking fighter stayed inside it for the whole landing tick (0.22 to 0.24 m apart; the next tick pushed them apart, so it lasted exactly one tick in every case found). In the test seed 5 was a thrown enemy landing on the standing player, seed 9 the thrown player landing on a walking enemy.
- Body fix (`MatchSim.separate`): a THROWN body counts as flying only while it is above its footing or rising; once it is at its footing and not rising (the same test that lands it in `afterCollision`) it is pushed apart like any body on that tick. The push, the height test (1.25 m) and the clinch, hold and grapple exceptions are unchanged; a body still in flight passes over the others as before.
- Balance: no combat number changed. The simulation changes only on the landing tick of a throw that lands inside another body.

- Method (probes were temp files, not kept in the repo; each can become a self-test): A. The game script run in a stub browser; a `Fighter` per roster body, state ATTACK, the move set the way `startAttack` does (`moveSpeedMult`, `mStartup`, `mActive`, `mRecovery`), `moveTick` stepped over the active ticks, `computePose()` then `skeleton(0, 0, 0, 0, false)`, and the key points (`pts` 9 to 20 hands and feet, 21 to 23 the item's far end) read in the fighter's own frame (z ahead). B. `Combat.apply` wrapped to record the key point of the attacker's limb and the foe's position for every unblocked strike of 32 `SimRunner.run` matches (one fighter per style, each against the next and the fifth one along, seeds 100 and up, 25 s). C. `stringsFor(style)` for the 16 styles: move sets, rows, signature entries. D. The largest difference of each joint from the guard over a whole move, for every move of every roster body. E. Constants and CSS read as text; the touch layout formulas worked out by hand for 844 x 390 and 360 / 390 wide portrait.
- For P17-02: the number to bring down is the gap of F01. A self-test can take Method A as it is (for each of the 32 bodies and each move: the limb tip at the first active tick within a set distance of the front of the volume, and not past the foe's centre; plus the height class of F03). The choices are to lengthen the visible reach (lean and step into the strike, `rootFwd`, longer arm and leg travel), to cut `reach` and `radius` (changes every balance number and fingerprint of P14-01 and the AI spacing, so a re-measure with `SimRunner` and one re-record), or both; weapon swings (F16) already do the first. Changing `reach` before P18-03/04 forces that task's re-record to be done on the new numbers.

### P12-05 determinism audit (2026-11-07)

- Base: `main` at 8aa8c39 (P18-43 fight rules, P17-19 touch crouch and the P18-40 sweep are in; P18-05 difficulty is built, 1194ead). No game code and no test was changed, nothing was run (this pass is read-only: `rg` and reading only). AC-001 (equal checksums with Reduced motion on and off) is not verified: P12-05 stays open until T2 runs, and D08 stays open, so every statement about two machines giving different numbers is a reading of the code and of the engines' rules, not a measurement; the cross-engine rows (J01, J02) need the golden-hash test below on a real iPhone and a PC. Line numbers are `breakpoint.html` at this commit (1,178,607 bytes with LF and BOM, of 4,000,000).
- Scope: the task's wording (all gameplay randomness through the seeded RNG, no frame-rate-dependent logic, no `Math.random` in the simulation, no viewer setting that changes the sim) plus what a peer would compute differently: clocks, locale, screen size and pixel ratio, quality, camera, DOM, pause, iteration order, sort stability, floating-point functions, input sampling. The sim is everything one `MatchSim.step` (11105) runs: `stepFight` 11151, `readIntents`, `Fighter.update` and `integrate`, `Combat`, `Arena.update`, items, hazards, fire, ring-out, waves, `AIController`.
- Result: 5 High, 6 Medium, 4 Low, 5 Informational (20 findings). Nothing found makes two runs of the same build on the same engine with the same seed and the same per-tick intents give different state: `Math.random` is used 0 times in the sim, `Date.now` and `performance.now` 0 times inside a tick, `Settings.v` inside a tick only in `animate`'s pose and trail code (6336, 6372, 6537, 6569, 6755), which no sim field reads, `dt` other than `DT` 0 times, and the AI reads nothing that is only drawn. What blocks online play is what is missing around the sim (a state hash, a way to save and load state, a tick driver that is not the wall clock, a wire form of the input) and one unmeasured risk across engines (J01).

**Recommended automated tests (new task, after J03; the helper is `MatchSim.stateHash()` and a per-tick log of it)**

1. T1 `Determinism: per-tick state hash` - the same seed and the same scripted human intents (a 1800-tick script that walks, jabs, kicks, blocks, grabs, throws) twice, plus an AI against AI run in Free Fight, Brawl with waves and a ring-out level; equal hash at every tick, the first differing tick and field printed on failure.
2. T2 `Determinism: viewer settings` (AC-001) - one run per row of the matrix (Reduced motion on/off, Shake 0/1, Flashes off/reduced/on, Effects low/high, Quality low/high with `Quality.apply()`, Shadows, Trails, Movement mode, Auto-assist off with an input that never reads it): hash equal to the baseline at every tick. Closes row D08.
3. T3 `Determinism: frame rate` - drive `Game.frame(now)` with a fake clock at 30, 60, 144 fps and a jittered 20 to 90 fps, steps below `MAX_STEPS_PER_FRAME`, the same per-tick intents (fed through a controller that returns the recorded intent for `m.tick`): the hash at tick N equal in all.
4. T4 `Determinism: input replay` - record the intents of a keyboard-driven run (scripted `keydown` events) and replay them through the wire form of J06: equal hash.
5. T5 `Determinism: no outside input` - run once with `Math.random` replaced by a different generator, with `Date.now` and `performance.now` shifted by an hour and jittered, and with `navigator.language`, `devicePixelRatio` and the window size changed: hash equal (catches any future leak of a clock, a locale or a screen size).
6. T6 `Determinism: golden hashes` - five fixed matches (1v1, Free Fight with ring-out and hazards, Brawl with waves, a lineup, a thrown-body case) with the hash every 60 ticks recorded as constants; the owner runs the self-test on the iPhone and on the PC (add to P16-03): equal constants prove J01 is harmless on those engines, a mismatch names the first tick.
7. T7 `Determinism: source scan` - the test fetches `breakpoint.html`, finds every `Math.random`, `Date.now`, `performance.now`, `Settings.v` and `.sort(` and checks the line is in an allow-list of function names (draw, sound, input, start, menu); a new use in sim code fails with its line. Together with T5 this keeps the audit true after P17-10, P18-05 and the online tasks.

#### P12-05 result (2026-11-09, base e1b263a)

The read-only audit above was redone with `rg` on this base (no new `Math.random`, `Date.now`, `performance.now`, `Settings.v`, `Camera.` or `Quality.` use in any code a tick runs; no `for in`, `Set` or `Map` loop in a tick) and then proven by a run. One code fix, one test, one comment. AC-001 is met: the test plays a scripted person against a Hard CPU in a Free Fight (warehouse, items, hazards; every breakable and the deck broken at tick 120) and a four-fighter brawl on the Pit (everything breakable broken at tick 200), takes one checksum per tick (every fighter's position, speed, knock-back, yaw, hp, stamina, state, move, momentum, burn, blind, item; every level object's hp and state; every loose item's place, speed, mode and wear; every hazard's state and timer; the tick, the phase, the round, the wins, the clock, the hit stop and the two id counters) and requires the same list from every other run: again; Reduced motion on; Reduced motion with its effect rows; every viewer setting flipped together; and each of the 14 settings flipped alone (Movement mode only shows that the sim never reads it: the scripted seat writes `fwd` and `side` itself, so the stick conversion in `PlayerInput.toFighterFrame` never runs); `Math.random`, `Date.now` and `performance.now` are replaced in exactly two runs, "every viewer setting flipped" and "clocks and Math.random replaced". It also requires the low quality preset to throw fewer debris pieces than the high one (so the cap was exercised) and the checksum to move (so the scenario plays). Checked by breaking the game on purpose in a scratch copy: a hit stop that Reduced motion shortens fails at tick 146, Auto-assist leaking into the intent fails at tick 19, a deck piece draw skipped on a low quality cap fails at tick 135 (duel) and tick 200 (brawl), and removing the counter reset fails at tick 0.

Replaced in the test |

Fingerprints: none moved (the counter reset changes no id comparison). The new test is `Determinism: viewer settings, clocks and Math.random never change the simulation`; T2 above is now done, T1 and T3 to T7 stay with the online tasks.

### P18-46 performance profile and plan (2026-11-07)

- Scope: read-only profile of `breakpoint.html` at `8aa8c39` (Chrome 157, i5-9600K, Windows 11). No repo file was changed. This is the plan for BP-P18-47.
- Method (P0-04, run from `file://`): Playwright Chrome, CDP `Emulation.setCPUThrottlingRate`, setting `quality` saved in `breakpoint.v1.settings`, `BREAKPOINT.benchmark(10, opts)` (1 s warm-up, 10 s measured, 3 runs per cell). Low-spec = viewport 640x360, throttle 4, quality `low` (render scale 0.6, 384x216). Desktop = 1280x720, throttle 1, quality `auto` (resolved to high, scale 1).
- Scenes: the P0-04 benchmark 1v1 (Expert vs Expert) and the same scene as a crowd brawl, `benchmark(10, { enemies: 6 })`. The crowd maximum is 7 fighters (`BRAWL_MAX_ENEMIES` = 6 plus the player), not 8. The benchmark picks `rooftop` today (most destructibles; fire and drop hazards; all objects smashed every 2 s, debris and particles at the quality cap), not `warehouse` as written in P0-04. A hazard scene is therefore covered by the benchmark itself; `subway`, `construction` and `pit` crowd brawls were measured on low-spec as a cross-check (below). Menu = main menu showcase, 6 s.
- Tools: (1) `performance.now()` wrappers around about 35 systems in a scratch copy of the game (`window.__bp` exposed; the copy is outside the repo); (2) CDP `Profiler` sampling at 200 us; (3) CDP `HeapProfiler` sampling (allocation by function); (4) Chrome trace with the V8 GC categories. Wrapper overhead inflates per-system times by roughly 15 to 25 %: use them for ranking and proportions, not as absolute values. Scratch files (temporary, may be gone): `C:\Users\GS\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\p1846\`. To repeat without them: (1) copy the game and insert `window.__bp = { Game, R, FX, Debris, Arena, Camera, Quality, Diag, Events, UI, Showcase, Settings, SimRunner, Tournament, Fighter, MatchSim, AIController, Combat, Music, Sound, Inputs }` before `window.BREAKPOINT = {`; wrap each listed method with a `performance.now()` sum and count (the `MatchSim.prototype` steps, `Fighter.prototype.animate`/`update`/`draw`/`computePose`/`walkSkeleton`, `AIController.prototype.think`, `Arena`/`Debris`/`FX` `update` and `draw`, `R.render`, `UI.update`/`frame`, `Inputs.update`, `Game.frame`, the WebGL calls and `navigator.getGamepads`); a frame over 12 ms logs every system that took over 0.8 ms of it. (2) CDP: `Emulation.setCPUThrottlingRate {rate: 4}`; `Profiler.setSamplingInterval {interval: 200}`, `Profiler.start`/`stop` around one benchmark; `HeapProfiler.startSampling {samplingInterval: 32768, includeObjectsCollectedByMajorGC: true, includeObjectsCollectedByMinorGC: true}` / `stopSampling` around the same 10 s; `Tracing.start` with categories `devtools.timeline`, `disabled-by-default-devtools.timeline`, `v8`, `disabled-by-default-v8.gc`, `blink.user_timing`. (3) Long frames and start-up: a `requestAnimationFrame` interval counter running beside `BREAKPOINT.benchmark(10, opts)` (the first second skipped, as the benchmark does), and an init script that records `performance.now()` at the first frame where `BREAKPOINT.diagnostics().state` is the menu.
- Not measured: GPU time (frame interval is pinned to 16.7 ms by vsync, so GPU headroom is unknown; draw calls are only 6 to 13, so the draw-call count is not a problem) and a real phone (P16-03).

- P0-04 pass rule (frame p95 <= 18 ms, work p95 <= 8 ms): met in every run; the one reading above 8 ms was a profiled run (8.3 to 8.5 ms with the Profiler attached). The game is not slow on average; what is left is headroom on a real phone (about 4x slower than this CPU, plus a GPU not measured here), single-frame spikes, and menu idle cost.
- Long frames (frame intervals over 20 ms in the 10 s after warm-up, runs 1 / 2 / 3 per row, no profiler or trace attached, 2026-11-07 11:00): low-spec 1v1 4 / 0 / 1 (max 35.8 ms); low-spec crowd 3 / 3 / 3 (max 36.1 ms); desktop 1v1 1 / 0 / 0 (max 21.0 ms); desktop crowd 1 / 0 / 0 (max 24.0 ms). In today's counter runs every low-spec long frame was one missed vsync (33 to 36 ms); the baseline runs above once reached 50.1 ms (two missed vsyncs); work spikes of 26 to 41 ms cause them. On desktop only the first run after a page load has one. The traced low-spec crowd run had 21 after its first 0.5 s (tracing adds cost).
- Start-up (navigation start to the first menu frame, served from the local preview, so no network time; a phone download of the 1.18 MB file comes on top): throttle 4 at 640x360 621 to 684 ms (script parsed and run by 271 to 290 ms; the boot routine `Diag.startupMs` 266 to 298 ms: renderer, pools, input, showcase); desktop 230 to 231 ms (boot 106 to 116 ms). Not a hotspot today; P18-47 keeps it in the benchmark result and checks it on a phone in P16-03.
- Allocation and GC (crowd, low-spec, 11 s trace; desktop GC not measured): the trace's V8 events show 2 scavenges (`MinorGC`, 7.4 ms total, max 3.9 ms) and 2 mark-compacts (`MajorGC`, 16 ms total, max 9.1 ms, with 52 incremental marking slices). Their used heap before and after (42.5 to 10.3, 37.5 to 10.8, 35.7 to 9.9, 21.7 to 10.2 MB) shows about 96 MB reclaimed in 11 s, about 8.7 MB/s or about 145 KB per frame; the young generation grows to about 30 MB before a scavenge, which is why there are only 2. The heap sampler's figure (about 182 KB per frame, about 11 MB/s, settings as in Tools) is of the same size and also counts what is still alive at the end. GC is 0.2 % of the time, but the two major GCs line up with the 25 to 35 ms frames that no system accounts for (spike log below). The 9.5 MB in the table is the benchmark's `performance.memory.usedJSHeapSize`, which Chrome rounds; the trace's used heap after each GC is 9.9 to 10.8 MB and does not grow, so there is no leak.
- Main-thread split (trace, low-spec crowd, 10 s): animation-frame callbacks 3.7 s of 10 s at 4x; style recalculation 0.42 s, layout 0.11 s, paint 0.08 s (the HUD DOM is about 5 % of the thread).
- Sim cost without rendering (`BREAKPOINT.simulate`, desktop): 22 to 35 us per tick (warehouse 35, rooftop 29, dojo 22, subway 25). A Tournament of 8 = 7 CPU matches = 648 ms, 28,148 ticks (about 90 ms per match as one uninterrupted task, about 360 ms at throttle 4). A 16-bracket is 15 matches. Of one headless match (160 ms instrumented): `Fighter.animate` 34 %, `readIntents` (AI) 15 %, `updateFighters` 9 %, `physics` 6 %.
